verses.1:1: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel on the other side of the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah facing Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
verses.1:2: It is eleven days from Horeb, by the way of Mount Seir, as far as Kadesh-barnea.
verses.1:3: Now it happened in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first of the month, that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel according to all that the LORD had commanded him regarding them,
verses.1:4: after he had struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
verses.1:5: On the other side of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses resolved to explain this law, saying:
verses.1:6: The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, "You have stayed at this mountain long enough.
verses.1:7: Turn and set out, and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Negev, and by the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates River.
verses.1:8: Look, I have put the land before you. Go in and possess the land that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them."
verses.1:9: Then I spoke to you at that time, saying, "I am unable to bear you alone.
verses.1:10: The LORD your God has multiplied you, and here you are today, like the stars of the heavens in multitude.
verses.1:11: May the LORD, the God of your fathers, add to you a thousand times as many as you are and bless you, just as He has spoken to you!
verses.1:12: How can I bear by myself your trouble, your burden, and your disputes?
verses.1:13: Bring forward for yourselves wise, discerning, and well-known men for your tribes, and I will set them as your heads."
verses.1:14: Then you answered me and said, "The thing you have spoken is good to do."
verses.1:15: So I took the heads of your tribes, men who were wise and well-known, and made them heads over you: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes.
verses.1:16: And I commanded your judges at that time, saying, "Hear disputes between your brothers and judge with righteousness between a man and his brother or the resident alien with him.
verses.1:17: You shall not show favoritism in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great equally. You shall not dread any man, for judgment belongs to God. And the matter that is too difficult for you, you shall bring before me, and I will hear it."
verses.1:18: And at that time I commanded you all the things that you were to do.
verses.1:19: Then we set out from Horeb and walked through all that great and fearsome wilderness you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, just as the LORD our God commanded us, and we came as far as Kadesh-barnea.
verses.1:20: Then I said to you, "You have come as far as the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving to us.
verses.1:21: Look, the LORD your God has put the land before you. Go up, possess it, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has spoken to you. Do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed."
verses.1:22: Then all of you drew near to me and said, "Let us send men ahead of us so that they may explore the land for us and bring word back to us about the way by which we should go up and the cities to which we will come."
verses.1:23: The matter seemed good in my eyes, so I took twelve men from you, one man for each tribe.
verses.1:24: They turned and went up into the hill country, came as far as the Valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.
verses.1:25: They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and they brought word back to us and said, "The land that the LORD our God is giving to us is good."
verses.1:26: Yet you were unwilling to go up, and you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
verses.1:27: You grumbled in your tents and said, "Because the LORD hates us, He brought us out from the land of Egypt to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.
verses.1:28: Where are we going up? Our brothers have caused our hearts to melt, saying, 'The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified up to the heavens; and moreover we saw sons of the Anakim there.'"
verses.1:29: And I said to you, "Do not be terrified and do not be afraid of them.
verses.1:30: The LORD your God, who goes before you, He Himself will fight for you, according to all that He did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
verses.1:31: and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, just as a man carries his son, along the entire way you walked until you reached this place."
verses.1:32: Yet despite this word, you did not trust in the LORD your God,
verses.1:33: who went before you along the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way in which you should walk, and in the cloud by day.
verses.1:34: And the LORD heard the sound of your words; He grew angry and swore, saying,
verses.1:35: "Not a man among these men, this evil generation, shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers,
verses.1:36: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him I will give the land on which he trod, and to his sons, because he followed the LORD completely."
verses.1:37: Even with me the LORD grew angry because of you, saying, "You too shall not enter there.
verses.1:38: Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall enter there. Strengthen him, for he will give it to Israel as an inheritance.
verses.1:39: And your little ones, who you said would become plunder, and your children, who today do not know good and evil, they shall enter there, and to them I will give it, and they shall possess it.
verses.1:40: But you, turn back and set out into the wilderness along the way of the Sea of Reeds."
verses.1:41: Then you answered and said to me, "We have sinned against the LORD. We ourselves will go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us." Then each of you strapped on his weapons of war, and you considered it a light thing to go up into the hill country.
verses.1:42: And the LORD said to me, "Say to them, 'Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not in your midst, so that you will not be struck down before your enemies.'"
verses.1:43: So I spoke to you, yet you did not listen; you rebelled against the command of the LORD, and you acted arrogantly and went up into the hill country.
verses.1:44: Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and pursued you just as bees do, and they crushed you in Seir as far as Hormah.
verses.1:45: Then you came back and wept before the LORD, yet the LORD did not listen to your voice, nor did He pay attention to you.
verses.1:46: So you stayed at Kadesh many days, for as many days as you stayed.
verses.2:1: Then we turned and traveled toward the wilderness along the road to the Sea of Reeds, just as the LORD had spoken to me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.
verses.2:2: Then the LORD said to me:
verses.2:3: "You have gone around this mountain long enough; turn yourselves northward.
verses.2:4: And command the people, saying, 'You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir. They will fear you, so guard yourselves very closely.
verses.2:5: Do not engage them in conflict, for I will not give you any of their land—not even a stepping place for the sole of a foot—because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.
verses.2:6: You shall buy food from them with silver and eat, and you shall also purchase water from them with silver and drink.
verses.2:7: For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand; He has known your walking through this great wilderness. Throughout these forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have not lacked anything.'"
verses.2:8: So we passed on from our brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the Arabah road, from Elath and from Ezion-geber; then we turned and passed along the road to the wilderness of Moab.
verses.2:9: Then the LORD said to me, "Do not show hostility toward Moab, and do not engage them in battle, for I will not give you any of its land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as a possession."
verses.2:10: The Emim lived in it formerly, a people great and numerous and tall like the Anakim.
verses.2:11: They too are reckoned as Rephaim, like the Anakim, though the Moabites call them Emim.
verses.2:12: And in Seir the Horites lived formerly, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them, and destroyed them from before themselves, and lived in their place, just as Israel did to the land of its possession that the LORD gave to them.
verses.2:13: "Now rise up and cross the Wadi Zered for yourselves." So we crossed the Wadi Zered.
verses.2:14: And the days that we traveled from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Wadi Zered totaled thirty-eight years, until the entire generation—the men of war—had perished from the midst of the camp, just as the LORD had sworn to them.
verses.2:15: Moreover, the hand of the LORD was against them to rout them from the midst of the camp until they perished.
verses.2:16: So it happened, when all the men of war had finished dying from the midst of the people,
verses.2:17: that the LORD spoke to me, saying:
verses.2:18: "This day you are crossing the border of Moab, at Ar.
verses.2:19: When you draw near opposite the sons of Ammon, do not show hostility toward them and do not engage them in conflict, for I will not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as a possession."
verses.2:20: It too is reckoned as a land of Rephaim; Rephaim lived in it formerly, though the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
verses.2:21: a people great and numerous and tall like the Anakim. Yet the LORD destroyed them from before them, and they dispossessed them and lived in their place,
verses.2:22: just as He did for the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites from before them, and they dispossessed them and have lived in their place until this day.
verses.2:23: And as for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who came out from Caphtor, destroyed them and lived in their place.
verses.2:24: "Rise up, set out, and cross the Wadi Arnon! Look, I have given into your hand Sihon king of Heshbon, the Amorite, and his land. Begin to take possession, and engage him in battle.
verses.2:25: This day I will begin to place the dread of you and the fear of you upon the peoples beneath all the heavens, who will hear the report of you and will quake and writhe before you."
verses.2:26: Then I dispatched messengers from the Wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with words of peace, saying:
verses.2:27: "Let me pass through your land. I will walk strictly along the road; I will not turn aside right or left.
verses.2:28: Sell me food for silver and I will eat, and give me water for silver and I will drink—just let me pass through on foot,
verses.2:29: just as the sons of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving to us."
verses.2:30: Yet Sihon, king of Heshbon, was not willing to let us pass by him, for the LORD your God made his spirit stiff and made his heart stubborn, so as to give him into your hand, as it is this day.
verses.2:31: Then the LORD said to me, "Look, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over before you. Begin—take possession, to possess his land."
verses.2:32: Then Sihon came out to meet us—he and all his people—for battle at Jahaz.
verses.2:33: And the LORD our God gave him over before us, and we struck down him and his sons and all his people.
verses.2:34: So we captured all his cities at that time and devoted to complete destruction every city—men, women, and little ones; we left no survivor.
verses.2:35: Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, together with the spoil of the cities that we captured.
verses.2:36: From Aroer, which is on the rim of the Wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the wadi, all the way to Gilead, there was not a town that stood too high for us; the LORD our God gave all of it over before us.
verses.2:37: Only to the land of the sons of Ammon you did not draw near—all along the side of the Wadi Jabbok, and the cities of the hill country, and all that the LORD our God had commanded.
verses.3:1: Then we turned and went up along the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came out to meet us—he and all his people—for battle at Edrei.
verses.3:2: Then the LORD said to me, "Do not be afraid of him, for into your hand I have given him, along with all his people and his land; and you shall do to him just as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
verses.3:3: So the LORD our God also gave into our hand Og, king of Bashan, and all his people, and we struck him down until no survivor was left to him.
verses.3:4: And we captured all his cities at that time; there was not a town that we did not take from them—sixty cities, the entire district of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
verses.3:5: All these were fortified cities with high walls, double gates, and bars, apart from very many unwalled cities.
verses.3:6: And we devoted them to complete destruction, just as we had done to Sihon, king of Heshbon, devoting to complete destruction every city—men, women, and little ones.
verses.3:7: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
verses.3:8: So at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon.
verses.3:9: The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir.
verses.3:10: All the cities of the tableland, along with all Gilead and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei—the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
verses.3:11: For only Og, king of Bashan, was left from the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bed was a bed of iron—is it not in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon? Nine cubits is its length and four cubits its width, by a man's cubit.
verses.3:12: So we took possession of this land at that time: from Aroer, which is beside the Wadi Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
verses.3:13: And the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh—the entire district of Argob, with all Bashan; that is called the land of Rephaim.
verses.3:14: Jair the son of Manasseh took the entire district of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and named them—that is, Bashan—after his own name, Havvoth-jair, until this day.
verses.3:15: And I gave Gilead to Machir.
verses.3:16: And to the Reubenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gilead even to the Wadi Arnon—the middle of the wadi as a border—and as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon,
verses.3:17: as well as the Arabah, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth even to the Sea of the Arabah—the Salt Sea—below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
verses.3:18: Then I commanded you at that time, saying, "The LORD your God has given you this land to possess it. You shall cross over armed for battle ahead of your brothers, the sons of Israel—all the men of valor.
verses.3:19: Only your wives, your little ones, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—shall remain in your cities that I have given to you,
verses.3:20: until the LORD gives rest to your brothers, just as to you, and they too take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving to them beyond the Jordan. Then you shall return, each man to his possession that I have given to you."
verses.3:21: And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, "Your own eyes have seen everything that the LORD your God did to these two kings; thus the LORD will do to all the kingdoms where you are crossing over.
verses.3:22: You must not fear them, for the LORD your God—He is the one who fights for you."
verses.3:23: Then I implored the LORD at that time, saying:
verses.3:24: "Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand; for what god is there in the heavens or on the earth who can do anything like Your works and Your mighty deeds?
verses.3:25: Please let me cross over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon."
verses.3:26: Yet the LORD was furious with me on your account and did not listen to me. And the LORD said to me, "Enough for you! Do not speak to Me any further about this matter.
verses.3:27: Go up to the summit of Pisgah and lift your eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, and see with your own eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.
verses.3:28: And command Joshua, strengthen him, and encourage him, for he will cross over ahead of this people, and he will cause them to inherit the land that you will see."
verses.3:29: And we stayed in the valley facing Beth-peor.
verses.4:1: And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the judgments that I am teaching you to carry out, so that you may live and enter and possess the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving to you.
verses.4:2: You must not add to the word that I am commanding you, and you must not subtract from it, in order to keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I am commanding you.
verses.4:3: Your very eyes saw what the LORD did at Baal-peor, for every man who walked after Baal-peor, the LORD your God wiped him out from your midst.
verses.4:4: Yet you who cling to the LORD your God, all of you are alive today.
verses.4:5: Look, I have taught you statutes and judgments, just as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you do so in the midst of the land that you are entering to possess.
verses.4:6: Keep them and carry them out, for this is your wisdom and your discernment in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, "Truly, a wise and discerning people is this great nation."
verses.4:7: For what great nation is there that has a god so close to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to Him?
verses.4:8: And what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments as righteous as all this law that I am placing before you today?
verses.4:9: Only watch yourself and guard your soul very carefully, so that you do not forget the things your eyes saw and so that they do not depart from your heart all the days of your life; and make them known to your children and to your children's children—
verses.4:10: the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, "Assemble the people to Me, and I will let them hear My words, so that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live on the earth, and that they may teach their children."
verses.4:11: Then you drew near and stood at the foot of the mountain, while the mountain was burning with fire up to the heart of the heavens—darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
verses.4:12: And the LORD spoke to you from within the fire. You were hearing the sound of words, yet you were seeing no form—only a voice.
verses.4:13: He declared to you His covenant that He commanded you to carry out—the ten words—and He wrote them on two stone tablets.
verses.4:14: And at that time the LORD commanded me to teach you statutes and judgments, for you to carry them out in the land that you are crossing over to possess.
verses.4:15: So watch very carefully over your souls, since you did not see any form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from within the fire,
verses.4:16: so that you do not act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, the form of any statue, the figure of male or female,
verses.4:17: the figure of any animal that is on the earth, the figure of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
verses.4:18: the figure of anything creeping on the ground, the figure of any fish that is in the waters below the earth;
verses.4:19: and so that you do not lift your eyes toward the heavens and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens, and be led astray and bow down to them and serve them—those that the LORD your God has apportioned to all the peoples beneath all the heavens.
verses.4:20: But the LORD took you and brought you out from the iron furnace, from Egypt, to become a people of inheritance for Him, as on this day.
verses.4:21: Now the LORD grew angry with me on account of you, and He swore that I would not cross over the Jordan and would not go into the good land that the LORD your God is giving to you as an inheritance.
verses.4:22: For I am going to die in this land; I am not crossing over the Jordan. Yet you are crossing over and will possess this good land.
verses.4:23: Be on guard for yourselves, so that you do not forget the covenant of the LORD your God that He made with you and make for yourselves a carved image—a form of anything the LORD your God has forbidden you.
verses.4:24: For the LORD your God—He is a devouring fire, a jealous God.
verses.4:25: When you have children and children's children and grow old in the land, and act corruptly and make a carved image—a form of anything—and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God to provoke Him to anger,
verses.4:26: I summon the heavens and the earth to witness against you today that you will surely perish swiftly from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not prolong your days on it, for you will certainly be wiped out.
verses.4:27: And the LORD will disperse you among the peoples, and you will remain few in number among the nations where the LORD will drive you.
verses.4:28: And there you will serve gods, the work of human hands—wood and stone—that do not see and do not hear and do not eat and do not smell.
verses.4:29: Yet from there you will seek the LORD your God and find Him, when you search for Him with your whole heart and with your whole soul.
verses.4:30: In your distress, when all these things find you in the latter days, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice.
verses.4:31: For the LORD your God is a compassionate God; He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant of your fathers that He swore to them.
verses.4:32: For inquire now about earlier days that were before you, since the day God created mankind on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: has anything like this great thing ever occurred, or has anything like it been heard?
verses.4:33: Has any people heard the voice of God speaking from within the fire, just as you yourself heard, and lived?
verses.4:34: Or has a god ever attempted to come and take a nation for himself from the midst of another nation, with testings, with signs and wonders, with war, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
verses.4:35: You yourself were made to see, so that you would know that the LORD—He is God; there is no other apart from Him.
verses.4:36: From the heavens He caused you to hear His voice to discipline you, and on the earth He made you see His great fire, and you heard His words from within the fire.
verses.4:37: And because He loved your fathers and chose their seed after them, He brought you out by His presence, with His great strength, from Egypt,
verses.4:38: to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, to give to you their land as an inheritance, as on this day.
verses.4:39: So know today, and bring it back to your heart, that the LORD—He is God in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is no other.
verses.4:40: And keep His statutes and His commandments that I am commanding you today, so that it may be well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may prolong your days on the land that the LORD your God is giving to you for all time.
verses.4:41: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
verses.4:42: for a killer to flee there who kills his neighbor unintentionally and had not hated him previously, so that he might flee to one of these cities and live:
verses.4:43: Bezer in the wilderness, in the land of the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
verses.4:44: And this is the law that Moses placed before the sons of Israel.
verses.4:45: These are the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt,
verses.4:46: beyond the Jordan, in the valley facing Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who resided in Heshbon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel struck down when they came out of Egypt.
verses.4:47: And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan—the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise—
verses.4:48: from Aroer, which is on the rim of the Wadi Arnon, as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,
verses.4:49: and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastward, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, beneath the slopes of Pisgah.
verses.5:1: Moses called to all Israel and said to them, "Listen, Israel, to the statutes and the judgments that I am speaking in your ears today; learn them and take care to carry them out.
verses.5:2: The LORD our God cut a covenant with us at Horeb.
verses.5:3: It was not with our fathers that the LORD cut this covenant, but with us—we who are here today, all of us alive.
verses.5:4: Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from within the fire—
verses.5:5: I was standing between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up on the mountain—saying,
verses.5:6: 'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
verses.5:7: You must not have other gods in My presence.
verses.5:8: You must not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
verses.5:9: You must not bow down to them or serve them, because I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the guilt of fathers upon children, and upon the third and upon the fourth generations of those who hate Me,
verses.5:10: yet showing loyal love to thousands, to those who love Me and to those who keep My commandments.
verses.5:11: You must not take up the name of the LORD your God in vain, because the LORD will not acquit the one who takes up His name in vain.
verses.5:12: Keep the Sabbath day to consecrate it, just as the LORD your God commanded you.
verses.5:13: Six days you are to labor and carry out all your work,
verses.5:14: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God; you must not do any work—you, or your son, or your daughter, or your male slave, or your female slave, or your ox, or your donkey, or any of your livestock, or your foreign resident who is within your gates—so that your male slave and your female slave may rest just like you.
verses.5:15: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm. For this reason the LORD your God has commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
verses.5:16: Honor your father and your mother, just as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged and so that things may go well for you upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.5:17: And you must not commit adultery.
verses.5:20: And you must not testify against your neighbor as a false witness.
verses.5:21: And you must not covet your neighbor's wife, and you must not crave your neighbor's house, his field, his male slave or his female slave, his ox or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.'
verses.5:22: These words the LORD spoke to your entire assembly on the mountain from within the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a loud voice, and He added nothing more. Then He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
verses.5:23: And when you heard the voice from within the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, you drew near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.
verses.5:24: And you said, 'Look, the LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and His voice we have heard from within the fire. This day we have seen that God speaks with man and he remains alive.
verses.5:25: And now, why should we die? For this great fire will devour us. If we continue hearing the voice of the LORD our God any further, we will die.
verses.5:26: For who among all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking from within the fire, as we have, and stayed alive?
verses.5:27: You draw near and listen to everything that the LORD our God says, and you speak to us everything that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will listen and do it.'
verses.5:28: Then the LORD heard the sound of your words as you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard the sound of the words of this people that they spoke to you; they have done well in all they have spoken.
verses.5:29: If only they had this heart in them to fear Me and to keep all My commandments always, so that things might go well for them and for their children forever!
verses.5:30: Go, tell them, "Go back to your tents."
verses.5:31: But as for you, stand here with Me, so that I may speak to you the entire commandment and the statutes and the judgments that you are to teach them, so that they may carry them out in the land that I am giving them to possess.'
verses.5:32: Therefore take care to do just as the LORD your God commanded you; you must not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.5:33: You must walk in the entire way that the LORD your God commanded you, so that you may live, and so that things may go well for you, and you may lengthen your days in the land that you will possess."
verses.6:1: Now this is the commandment, the statutes and the judgments, that the LORD your God commanded to be taught to you, to carry out in the land to which you are crossing over to possess it,
verses.6:2: so that you may fear the LORD your God—to keep all His statutes and His commandments that I am commanding you, you and your son and your son's son, all the days of your life—and so that your days may be prolonged.
verses.6:3: So listen, Israel, and take care to do so, that things may go well for you and that you may multiply greatly, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you—a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.6:4: Listen, Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD is one.
verses.6:5: And you must love the LORD your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with all your might.
verses.6:6: And these words that I am commanding you today must be upon your heart.
verses.6:7: You must teach them repeatedly to your children and speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk along the way, and when you lie down, and when you get up.
verses.6:8: You must tie them as a sign upon your hand, and they are to be frontlets between your eyes.
verses.6:9: And you must write them upon the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
verses.6:10: And it will happen when the LORD your God brings you into the land that He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to you—great and good cities that you did not build,
verses.6:11: and houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, and hewn cisterns that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,
verses.6:12: then guard yourself so that you do not forget the LORD, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
verses.6:13: The LORD your God you must fear, and Him you must serve, and by His name you must swear.
verses.6:14: You must not go after other gods, from among the gods of the peoples who are all around you,
verses.6:15: for the LORD your God among you is a jealous God—or else the anger of the LORD your God will burn against you, and He will destroy you from the face of the earth.
verses.6:16: You must not test the LORD your God, just as you tested Him at Massah.
verses.6:17: You must carefully keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and His testimonies and His statutes that He commanded you.
verses.6:18: And you must do what is upright and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that things may go well for you, and so that you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD swore to your fathers,
verses.6:19: by thrusting out all your enemies from your presence, just as the LORD spoke.
verses.6:20: When your son asks you in the future, saying, "What are the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments that the LORD our God commanded you?"
verses.6:21: then you must say to your son, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.6:22: And the LORD displayed signs and wonders, great and devastating, against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against his entire household, before our eyes.
verses.6:23: And He brought us out from there so that He might bring us in, to give us the land that He swore to our fathers.
verses.6:24: And the LORD commanded us to carry out all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God for our good always, to keep us alive just as on this day.
verses.6:25: And righteousness will be ours if we take care to carry out this entire commandment before the LORD our God, just as He commanded us."
verses.7:1: When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to take possession of, and He dislodges many nations from before you—the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—seven nations more numerous and more powerful than you,
verses.7:2: and when the LORD your God gives them over before you and you strike them down, you must wholly devote them to destruction. You must not make a covenant with them, and you must not show them favor.
verses.7:3: You must not intermarry with them: you must not give your daughter to his son, nor take his daughter for your son.
verses.7:4: For he will turn your son away from following Me, and they will serve other gods; then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will swiftly wipe you out.
verses.7:5: Instead, this is what you must do to them: you must pull down their altars, shatter their standing stones, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images in the fire.
verses.7:6: For you are a holy people for the LORD your God; it is you whom the LORD your God has chosen to be a treasured people for Himself from among all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
verses.7:7: It was not because you were more numerous than all the peoples that the LORD set His affection on you and chose you, since you were the fewest among all the peoples.
verses.7:8: Rather, because of the LORD's love for you and because He kept the oath He swore to your fathers, the LORD brought you out by a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slaves, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
verses.7:9: So you must know that the LORD your God—He is God, the faithful God who keeps the covenant and loyal love for those who love Him and for those who keep His commandments, to a thousand generations,
verses.7:10: and who repays those who hate Him to their face in order to destroy them; He will not delay with one who hates Him—to his face He will repay him.
verses.7:11: So you must keep the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that I command you today, by doing them.
verses.7:12: Then it will happen that because you listen to these judgments, and keep them and do them, the LORD your God will keep for you the covenant and the loyal love that He swore to your fathers.
verses.7:13: He will love you, bless you, and make you numerous; He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your soil—your grain, your new wine, and your fresh oil, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock—on the land that He swore to your fathers to give you.
verses.7:14: You will be blessed more than all the peoples; there will be neither barren male nor barren female among you, nor among your livestock.
verses.7:15: The LORD will remove every illness from you, and He will not place on you any of the dreadful diseases of Egypt that you knew, but will put them on all those who hate you.
verses.7:16: You must devour all the peoples whom the LORD your God is giving to you; your eye must show no pity on them, and you must not serve their gods, for that will be a snare to you.
verses.7:17: If you say in your heart, "These nations are more numerous than I am; how will I be able to dispossess them?"
verses.7:18: you must not be afraid of them; be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:
verses.7:19: the great tests that your eyes saw, the signs and the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm, with which the LORD your God brought you out; in the same way the LORD your God will do to all the peoples before whom you are afraid.
verses.7:20: Furthermore, the LORD your God will send the hornet among them until those who remain and those who hide themselves from before you perish.
verses.7:21: You must not be terrified before them, because the LORD your God is among you—a great and fearsome God.
verses.7:22: The LORD your God will dislodge these nations from before you little by little; you will not be able to finish them off swiftly, or else the wild animals of the field will multiply against you.
verses.7:23: But the LORD your God will give them over before you and throw them into a massive panic until they are wiped out.
verses.7:24: He will put their kings into your hand, and you will cause their name to perish from beneath the heavens; no man will stand firm before you until you have wiped them out.
verses.7:25: You must burn the carved images of their gods in the fire. Do not covet the silver and gold on them and take it for yourself, so that you are not ensnared by it; for it is a detestable thing to the LORD your God.
verses.7:26: You must not bring a detestable thing into your house, or you will become a thing devoted to destruction just like it; you must completely loathe it and completely detest it, for it is a thing devoted to destruction.
verses.8:1: The entire commandment that I am commanding you today you must take care to do, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your fathers.
verses.8:2: And you must remember the entire way along which the LORD your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart—whether you would keep His commandments or not.
verses.8:3: So He humbled you, caused you to go hungry, and fed you the manna that you did not know and your fathers did not know, in order to make you know that not on bread alone does a human being live, but on everything that goes forth from the mouth of the LORD does a human being live.
verses.8:4: Your garment did not wear away on you, and your foot did not become swollen these forty years.
verses.8:5: You must know within your heart, then, that just as a man disciplines his son, the LORD your God is disciplining you.
verses.8:6: So keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and fearing Him.
verses.8:7: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of springs and deep waters flowing out in the valley and in the hill country;
verses.8:8: a land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of oil-bearing olives and honey;
verses.8:9: a land where you will not eat bread in scarcity and will not lack anything in it; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose mountains you will mine copper.
verses.8:10: Once you have eaten and are satisfied, you must bless the LORD your God on account of the good land that He gave you.
verses.8:11: Watch yourself so that you do not forget the LORD your God by failing to keep His commandments, His judgments, and His statutes that I command you today;
verses.8:12: or else, after you have eaten and are satisfied, and build good houses and inhabit them,
verses.8:13: and your cattle and your flock multiply, and silver and gold multiply for you, and everything that belongs to you multiplies,
verses.8:14: then your heart will become lifted up, and you will forget the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves,
verses.8:15: who led you through the great and fearsome wilderness of fiery serpents, scorpions, and parched ground where there was no water; who brought water out for you from the flint rock,
verses.8:16: who fed you manna in the wilderness that your fathers did not know, in order to humble you and in order to test you, so as to do good to you in your future;
verses.8:17: and you will say in your heart, "My strength and the might of my hand have produced this wealth for me."
verses.8:18: Rather, you must remember the LORD your God, for it is He who gives you strength to produce wealth, in order to uphold His covenant that He swore to your fathers, as it is today.
verses.8:19: And it will come about that if you indeed forget the LORD your God, and walk after other gods, and serve them and bow down to them, I bear witness against you today that you will certainly perish.
verses.8:20: Just like the nations whom the LORD is causing to perish from before you, in the same way you will perish, because you will not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
verses.9:1: Listen, Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan to go in and take possession of nations greater and mightier than you, large cities fortified up to the heavens,
verses.9:2: a great and tall people, the sons of the Anakim, whom you know and about whom you have heard, "Who can stand firm before the sons of Anak?"
verses.9:3: So know today that the LORD your God is the One crossing over ahead of you as a devouring fire; He will wipe them out, and He will subdue them before you. Then you will dispossess them and cause them to perish quickly, just as the LORD spoke to you.
verses.9:4: Do not say in your heart, when the LORD your God thrusts them out from before you, "Because of my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to take possession of this land." Rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is dispossessing them from before you.
verses.9:5: It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to take possession of their land; instead, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD your God is dispossessing them from before you, and in order to uphold the word that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
verses.9:6: So know that it is not on account of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving this good land to you to take possession of it, because you are a stiff-necked people.
verses.9:7: Remember, do not forget how you provoked the LORD your God to wrath in the wilderness; from the day you went out from the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.
verses.9:8: At Horeb as well, you provoked the LORD to wrath, and the LORD grew angry enough with you to wipe you out.
verses.9:9: When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD had made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water.
verses.9:10: Then the LORD gave to me the two stone tablets, written with the finger of God; on them were all the very words that the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from within the fire on the day of the assembly.
verses.9:11: At the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave to me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.
verses.9:12: And the LORD said to me, "Get up, go down quickly from here, because your people whom you brought out of Egypt have corrupted themselves. They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a cast image."
verses.9:13: Then the LORD said to me, "I have seen this people, and look, they are a stiff-necked people.
verses.9:14: Leave Me alone, so that I may wipe them out and erase their name from beneath the heavens; and I will make you into a nation mightier and more numerous than they."
verses.9:15: Then I turned and went down from the mountain, as the mountain was blazing with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my two hands.
verses.9:16: I saw, and look, you had sinned against the LORD your God: you had made for yourselves a cast calf; you had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
verses.9:17: So I grasped the two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and shattered them before your eyes.
verses.9:18: Then I fell prostrate before the LORD as at the first, forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water, on account of all your sin that you had sinned, in doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD to provoke Him to anger.
verses.9:19: For I dreaded the anger and fury with which the LORD was wrathful against you, so as to wipe you out. Yet the LORD listened to me that time as well.
verses.9:20: And the LORD grew very angry with Aaron, so as to wipe him out; so I prayed on behalf of Aaron as well at that time.
verses.9:21: Then I took your sin that you had made, the calf, and burned it in the fire; I pounded it, grinding it thoroughly until it became fine dust, and I threw its dust into the stream coming down from the mountain.
verses.9:22: And at Taberah, and at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, you kept provoking the LORD to wrath.
verses.9:23: And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, "Go up and take possession of the land that I have given to you," you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God; you did not trust Him, and you did not listen to His voice.
verses.9:24: You have been rebelling against the LORD since the day I knew you.
verses.9:25: So I fell prostrate before the LORD for the forty days and the forty nights that I prostrated myself, because the LORD had said He would wipe you out.
verses.9:26: And I prayed to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, whom You redeemed through Your greatness, whom You brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.9:27: Remember Your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not pay attention to the stubbornness of this people, or to their wickedness, or to their sin.
verses.9:28: Otherwise, the land from which You brought us out will say, 'Because the LORD was unable to bring them into the land that He spoke of to them, and because He hated them, He brought them out to put them to death in the wilderness.'
verses.9:29: Yet they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out with Your great strength and with Your outstretched arm."
verses.10:1: At that time the LORD said to me, "Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up to Me on the mountain, and make for yourself a wooden ark.
verses.10:2: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered, and you are to place them in the ark."
verses.10:3: So I made an ark of acacia wood, carved two stone tablets like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
verses.10:4: And He wrote on the tablets, like the first writing, the Ten Words that the LORD spoke to you on the mountain from within the fire on the day of the assembly; and the LORD gave them to me.
verses.10:5: Then I turned and went down from the mountain, and placed the tablets in the ark that I had made; and there they remain, just as the LORD commanded me.
verses.10:6: And the sons of Israel traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
verses.10:7: From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
verses.10:8: At that time the LORD separated the tribe of Levi to bear the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister to Him, and to bless in His name, down to this day.
verses.10:9: For this reason Levi has no share or inheritance with his brothers; the LORD Himself is his inheritance, just as the LORD your God spoke to him.
verses.10:10: And I remained on the mountain as during the first days, forty days and forty nights; and the LORD listened to me that time as well: the LORD was unwilling to destroy you.
verses.10:11: Then the LORD said to me, "Get up, go on the journey ahead of the people, so that they may enter and take possession of the land that I swore to their fathers to give to them."
verses.10:12: And now, Israel, what is the LORD your God asking from you, except to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the LORD your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul,
verses.10:13: to observe the commandments of the LORD and His statutes that I am commanding you today, for your own good?
verses.10:14: See, to the LORD your God belong the heavens and the heaven of heavens, the earth and everything that is in it.
verses.10:15: Yet the LORD fixed His affection on your fathers alone, to love them, and He chose their seed after them—you—out of all the peoples, as it is this day.
verses.10:16: So circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not stiffen your neck any longer.
verses.10:17: For the LORD your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the God who is great, mighty, and awe-inspiring, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.
verses.10:18: He carries out justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the foreign resident, giving him bread and clothing.
verses.10:19: Therefore you are to love the foreign resident, because you were foreign residents in the land of Egypt.
verses.10:20: The LORD your God you must fear; Him you must serve, and to Him you must cling, and by His name you must swear.
verses.10:21: He is your praise, and He is your God, who has done for you these great and awe-inspiring deeds that your eyes have seen.
verses.10:22: As seventy persons your fathers went down to Egypt, and now the LORD your God has made you like the stars of the heavens in multitude.
verses.11:1: So you shall love the LORD your God, and you shall keep His charge, His statutes, His judgments, and His commandments at all times.
verses.11:2: And know today—for I am not addressing your children, who have not known and who have not seen—the discipline of the LORD your God, His greatness, His strong hand, and His outstretched arm,
verses.11:3: and His signs and His deeds that He did in the midst of Egypt to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to all his land,
verses.11:4: and what He did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and to its chariots, how He made the waters of the Sea of Reeds flow over them as they pursued after you, and the LORD destroyed them to this day,
verses.11:5: and what He did for you in the wilderness until you arrived at this place,
verses.11:6: and what He did to Dathan and to Abiram, the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, along with their households, their tents, and every living thing that was at their feet in the midst of all Israel;
verses.11:7: for it is your own eyes that saw all the great work of the LORD that He did.
verses.11:8: So you shall keep the entire commandment that I am commanding you today, in order that you may be strong, and enter and possess the land that you are crossing over to possess,
verses.11:9: and in order that you may lengthen your days on the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their seed, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.11:10: For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where you would sow your seed and water it with your foot like a vegetable garden.
verses.11:11: Rather, the land that you are crossing over to possess is a land of mountains and valleys; it drinks water from the rain of the heavens,
verses.11:12: a land that the LORD your God looks after; continually the eyes of the LORD your God are upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
verses.11:13: And it will come about, if you carefully listen to My commandments that I am commanding you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
verses.11:14: that I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather your grain, your new wine, and your fresh oil.
verses.11:15: And I will give grass in your field for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
verses.11:16: Guard yourselves, or else your heart will be enticed, and you will turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them,
verses.11:17: and the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, and the ground will not give its yield, and you will perish quickly off the good land that the LORD is giving you.
verses.11:18: So you shall set these words of mine upon your heart and upon your soul, and you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
verses.11:19: And you shall teach them to your children, speaking about them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the road, when you lie down, and when you rise up.
verses.11:20: And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
verses.11:21: in order that your days and the days of your children may multiply on the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give them, like the days of the heavens above the earth.
verses.11:22: For if you carefully keep this entire commandment that I am commanding you to do, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to cling to Him,
verses.11:23: then the LORD will dispossess all these nations from before you, and you will dispossess nations larger and stronger than you.
verses.11:24: Every place where the sole of your foot treads will belong to you; from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the River Euphrates, as far as the western sea will be your territory.
verses.11:25: No one will stand firm before you; the LORD your God will put the dread of you and the fear of you over the face of all the land where you tread, just as He spoke to you.
verses.11:26: See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
verses.11:27: the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I am commanding you today,
verses.11:28: and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way that I am commanding you today to go after other gods that you have not known.
verses.11:29: And it will come about, when the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, that you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
verses.11:30: Are they not across the Jordan, beyond the road toward the setting sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
verses.11:31: For you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and you will possess it and live in it.
verses.11:32: And you shall be careful to do all the statutes and the judgments that I am setting before you today.
verses.12:1: These are the statutes and the judgments that you shall be careful to do in the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess, all the days that you live on the earth.
verses.12:2: You shall completely destroy all the places where the nations whom you are dispossessing served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every lush tree.
verses.12:3: And you shall tear down their altars, shatter their sacred pillars, and burn their Asherah poles with fire; and you shall cut down the carved images of their gods and destroy their name from that place.
verses.12:4: You shall not do like this to the LORD your God.
verses.12:5: Instead, you shall seek out the place that the LORD your God will choose from all your tribes to put His name there, His dwelling place, and there you shall come.
verses.12:6: And there you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, your vows and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.
verses.12:7: And there you shall eat before the LORD your God, and you shall rejoice in every undertaking of your hand, you and your households, in which the LORD your God has blessed you.
verses.12:8: You shall not do according to all that we are doing here today, each man whatever is right in his own eyes,
verses.12:9: for up to now you have not come to the resting place and to the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.12:10: But when you cross the Jordan and live in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to inherit, and He gives you rest from all your enemies on every side so that you live in security,
verses.12:11: then to the place that the LORD your God will choose to make His name dwell, there you shall bring all that I am commanding you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and all the choicest of your vows that you vow to the LORD.
verses.12:12: And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God, you, your sons and your daughters, your male slaves and your female slaves, and the Levite who is within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance with you.
verses.12:13: Guard yourself that you do not offer up your burnt offerings in every place that you see;
verses.12:14: rather, in the place that the LORD will choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer up your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I am commanding you.
verses.12:15: However, to the full desire of your soul you may slaughter and eat meat, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that He has given you within all your gates; the unclean and the clean may eat it, like the gazelle and like the deer.
verses.12:16: Only the blood you shall not eat; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
verses.12:17: You are not permitted to eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, your new wine, or your fresh oil, or the firstborn of your herd or your flock, or any of your vows that you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution of your hand;
verses.12:18: rather, you shall eat them before the LORD your God in the place that the LORD your God will choose—you, your son and your daughter, your male slave and your female slave, and the Levite who is within your gates—and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in every undertaking of your hand.
verses.12:19: Guard yourself that you do not forsake the Levite all your days on your land.
verses.12:20: When the LORD your God enlarges your territory, just as He spoke to you, and you say, "I will eat meat," because your soul desires to eat meat, then you may eat meat to the full desire of your soul.
verses.12:21: If the place that the LORD your God will choose to put His name there is too far from you, then you may slaughter from your herd and from your flock that the LORD has given you, just as I have commanded you, and you may eat within your gates to the full desire of your soul.
verses.12:22: Indeed, just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you may eat it; the unclean and the clean together may eat it.
verses.12:23: Only be firm not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the meat.
verses.12:24: You shall not eat it; onto the ground you shall pour it out like water.
verses.12:25: You shall not eat it, in order that it may go well for you and for your children after you, because you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.12:26: Only the holy things that are yours, and your vows, you shall carry and come to the place that the LORD will choose.
verses.12:27: And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood, on the altar of the LORD your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, and the meat you shall eat.
verses.12:28: Be careful to listen to all these words that I am commanding you, in order that it may go well for you and for your children after you forever, because you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
verses.12:29: When the LORD your God cuts off from before you the nations whom you are entering to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,
verses.12:30: guard yourself that you are not ensnared into following them after they are destroyed from before you, and that you do not inquire about their gods, saying, "How did these nations serve their gods, so that I too may do the same?"
verses.12:31: You shall not do like this to the LORD your God, for every abomination to the LORD that He hates they have done for their gods; indeed, even their sons and their daughters they burn in the fire for their gods.
verses.13:1: Every word that I am commanding you, you shall take care to do it; you shall not add to it, and you shall not subtract from it.
verses.13:2: If a prophet or a dreamer of a dream rises up in your midst and gives you a sign or a wonder,
verses.13:3: and the sign or the wonder comes to pass about which he spoke to you, saying, "Let us go after other gods"—whom you have not known—"and let us serve them,"
verses.13:4: you must not listen to the words of that prophet or to the dreamer of that dream, because the LORD your God is testing you to know whether you love the LORD your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul.
verses.13:5: You shall walk after the LORD your God, and you shall fear Him; you shall keep His commandments and listen to His voice; you shall serve Him and cling to Him.
verses.13:6: Now that prophet or the dreamer of that dream shall be put to death, because he spoke rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt and ransomed you from the house of slaves, to lead you astray from the path on which the LORD your God commanded you to walk. So you shall sweep away the evil from your midst.
verses.13:7: If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is like your own soul, incites you in secret, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods"—whom you have not known, you and your fathers,
verses.13:8: of the gods of the peoples around you, those near to you or those far from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth—
verses.13:9: you must not consent to him, nor listen to him; your eye must not spare him, nor must you show compassion or cover for him.
verses.13:10: Instead, you shall certainly kill him; your hand shall be against him first to put him to death, and the hand of all the people afterward.
verses.13:11: And you shall stone him with stones so that he dies, because he sought to lead you astray from the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
verses.13:12: And all Israel will hear and be afraid, and they will not again do anything like this evil thing in your midst.
verses.13:13: If you hear in one of your cities that the LORD your God is giving you to dwell there, saying,
verses.13:14: "Worthless men have gone out from your midst and have led the residents of their city astray, saying, 'Let us go and serve other gods'"—whom you have not known—
verses.13:15: then you shall inquire, examine, and question thoroughly; and look, if the matter is true and confirmed, that this abomination has been done in your midst,
verses.13:16: you shall certainly strike down the residents of that city with the edge of the sword, devoting it to destruction—along with everything that is in it and its livestock—with the edge of the sword.
verses.13:17: You shall gather all its plunder into the middle of its public square and burn the city and all its plunder with fire as a whole offering to the LORD your God. It shall become a ruin mound forever; it shall not be built again.
verses.13:18: Nothing from what is devoted to destruction shall cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from His burning anger and grant you compassion, show you mercy, and multiply you, just as He swore to your fathers,
verses.13:19: if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God by keeping all His commandments that I am commanding you today, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
verses.14:1: You are sons of the LORD your God. You shall not gash yourselves, nor make a bald spot between your eyes for the dead.
verses.14:2: Because you are a holy people to the LORD your God, and it is you whom the LORD has chosen to be for Him a treasured people out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
verses.14:3: You must not eat any abomination.
verses.14:4: These are the animals that you may eat: ox, sheep, and goat;
verses.14:5: deer, gazelle, fallow deer, wild goat, addax, oryx, and mountain sheep.
verses.14:6: And every animal that parts the hoof, having a cleft splitting it into two hooves, and chews the cud among the animals—that one you may eat.
verses.14:7: However, these you must not eat from among those that chew the cud or those that part the cleft hoof: the camel, the hare, and the rock hyrax, for although they chew the cud, they do not part the hoof; they are unclean to you.
verses.14:8: And the pig, because it parts the hoof yet does not chew the cud, is unclean to you. You shall not eat from their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses.
verses.14:9: These you may eat from all that are in the waters: everything that has fins and scales you may eat.
verses.14:10: Yet everything that does not have fins and scales you must not eat; it is unclean to you.
verses.14:11: Every clean bird you may eat.
verses.14:12: Yet these are the ones among them that you must not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, and the osprey;
verses.14:13: the buzzard, the falcon, and the kite according to its kind;
verses.14:14: every raven according to its kind;
verses.14:15: the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, and the hawk according to its kind;
verses.14:16: the little owl, the great owl, and the barn owl;
verses.14:17: the desert owl, the Egyptian vulture, and the cormorant;
verses.14:18: the stork, the heron according to its kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
verses.14:19: And every winged swarming creature is unclean to you; they must not be eaten.
verses.14:20: Every clean winged creature you may eat.
verses.14:21: You must not eat any animal that died naturally; you may give it to the resident alien who is within your gates so that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner, because you are a holy people to the LORD your God. You must not boil a young goat in the milk of its mother.
verses.14:22: You must certainly tithe all the produce of your seed that comes forth from the field year by year.
verses.14:23: And you shall eat before the LORD your God, in the place that He chooses to cause His name to dwell there, the tithe of your grain, your new wine, and your fresh oil, and the firstborn of your herd and your flock, in order that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
verses.14:24: And if the journey is too long for you, so that you cannot carry it, because the place that the LORD your God chooses to place His name there is too far from you when the LORD your God blesses you,
verses.14:25: then you shall trade it for silver, tie up the silver in your hand, and go to the place that the LORD your God chooses.
verses.14:26: You may spend the silver on whatever your soul longs for—on cattle or sheep, on wine or strong drink, or on anything your soul asks of you—and you shall eat there before the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
verses.14:27: And the Levite who is within your gates you must not forsake, because he has no share or inheritance with you.
verses.14:28: At the end of three years, you shall bring out the entire tithe of your produce in that year and store it within your gates.
verses.14:29: Then the Levite—because he has no share or inheritance with you—and the resident alien, the fatherless, and the widow who are within your gates shall come, eat, and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in every work of your hand that you do.
verses.15:1: At the end of seven years you shall observe a release.
verses.15:2: And these are the terms of the release: every holder of a loan shall release what he has lent to his neighbor; he must not demand payment from his neighbor or his brother, because a release to the LORD has been proclaimed.
verses.15:3: From a foreigner you may demand payment, but whatever belongs to you with your brother your hand shall release.
verses.15:4: Yet there will be no needy person among you, because the LORD will certainly bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,
verses.15:5: if only you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, taking care to perform this entire commandment that I am commanding you today.
verses.15:6: Because the LORD your God will bless you just as He promised you, you will lend to many nations, while you yourself will not borrow; and you will rule over many nations, yet over you they will not rule.
verses.15:7: If there is among you a needy person, one of your brothers in any of your gates within your land that the LORD your God is giving you, you must not harden your heart or clench your hand against your needy brother.
verses.15:8: Instead, you shall open your hand wide to him and surely lend him enough for his need, whatever he lacks.
verses.15:9: Watch yourself so that there is no worthless thought in your heart, saying, "The seventh year, the year of release, has drawn near," and your eye turns begrudging toward your needy brother and you give him nothing; then he will cry out against you to the LORD, and sin will be in you.
verses.15:10: You shall certainly give to him, and your heart must not be begrudging when you give to him; for on account of this matter the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything to which you put your hand.
verses.15:11: For the needy will never cease from the midst of the land; therefore I am commanding you, saying, "You shall open your hand wide to your brother, to your poor, and to your needy in your land."
verses.15:12: If your brother—a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman—is sold to you, he shall serve you for six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him away free from you.
verses.15:13: And when you send him away free from you, you must not send him away empty-handed.
verses.15:14: You shall supply him generously from your flock, from your threshing floor, and from your winepress; from what the LORD your God has blessed you with, you shall give to him.
verses.15:15: And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God ransomed you; therefore I am commanding you this matter today.
verses.15:16: And it shall be that if he says to you, "I will not go out from you"—because he loves you and your household, since it goes well for him with you—
verses.15:17: then you shall take the awl and put it through his ear and into the door, and he shall become your slave forever; and to your female slave also you shall do likewise.
verses.15:18: It must not seem hard in your eyes when you send him away free from you, because he has served you six years, worth double the wages of a hired worker; and the LORD your God will bless you in everything that you do.
verses.15:19: Every firstborn male that is born in your herd and in your flock you shall consecrate to the LORD your God. You must not work with the firstborn of your ox, and you must not shear the firstborn of your flock.
verses.15:20: Before the LORD your God you shall eat it year by year in the place that the LORD chooses, you and your household.
verses.15:21: Yet if there is a defect in it—if it is lame or blind, any severe defect—you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
verses.15:22: Within your gates you may eat it, the unclean and the clean together, like the gazelle and like the deer.
verses.15:23: Only its blood you must not eat; you shall pour it out onto the ground like water.
verses.16:1: Keep the month of Abib and celebrate Passover to the LORD your God, because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out from Egypt at night.
verses.16:2: You shall sacrifice Passover to the LORD your God, of flock and herd, in the place that the LORD will choose to cause His name to dwell there.
verses.16:3: You shall not eat anything leavened with it; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, bread of affliction, because you went out from the land of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day of your going out from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
verses.16:4: No leaven shall be seen with you within all your territory for seven days, and nothing of the meat that you sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall stay overnight until morning.
verses.16:5: You may not sacrifice the Passover in any one of your gates that the LORD your God is giving to you.
verses.16:6: Rather, at the place that the LORD your God will choose to cause His name to dwell, there you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening as the sun goes down, the appointed time of your going out from Egypt.
verses.16:7: You shall cook and eat in the place that the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents.
verses.16:8: Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God; you shall not do any work.
verses.16:9: Seven weeks you shall count for yourself; from the beginning of the sickle in the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
verses.16:10: Then you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with the measure of a freewill offering from your hand, which you shall give according to how the LORD your God blesses you.
verses.16:11: And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, the Levite who is in your gates, and the resident alien, the fatherless, and the widow who are in your midst—in the place that the LORD your God will choose to cause His name to dwell there.
verses.16:12: And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall keep and carry out these statutes.
verses.16:13: You shall celebrate the Feast of Booths for yourself for seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.
verses.16:14: And you shall rejoice in your feast—you, your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite, the resident alien, the fatherless, and the widow who are in your gates.
verses.16:15: For seven days you shall hold a feast to the LORD your God in the place that the LORD will choose, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your yield and in all the work of your hands, and you will be nothing but joyful.
verses.16:16: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the LORD your God in the place that He will choose: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Booths; and none shall appear before the LORD empty-handed.
verses.16:17: Each man shall give according to the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that He has given to you.
verses.16:18: You shall appoint judges and officials for yourself in all your gates that the LORD your God is giving to you throughout your tribes, and they shall judge the people with just judgment.
verses.16:19: You shall not bend justice; you shall not be partial, and you shall not accept a bribe, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and overturns the words of the righteous.
verses.16:20: Justice, justice you shall pursue, so that you may live and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving to you.
verses.16:21: You shall not plant for yourself an Asherah of any tree beside the altar of the LORD your God that you will make for yourself.
verses.16:22: And you shall not erect for yourself a standing stone, which the LORD your God hates.
verses.17:1: You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep in which there is a blemish, anything bad, because that is an abomination to the LORD your God.
verses.17:2: If there is found in your midst, in any one of your gates that the LORD your God is giving to you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, transgressing His covenant,
verses.17:3: and goes and serves other gods and bows down to them, or to the sun or to the moon or to any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded,
verses.17:4: and it is reported to you and you hear of it, you shall inquire thoroughly; and now, if it is true, the matter confirmed, that this abomination has been done in Israel,
verses.17:5: then you shall bring out that man or that woman who has done this evil thing to your gates—the man or the woman—and you shall stone them with stones, and they shall die.
verses.17:6: By the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses the one to die shall be put to death; he shall not be put to death by the testimony of one witness.
verses.17:7: The hand of the witnesses shall be upon him first to put him to death, and the hand of all the people last; and you shall purge the evil from your midst.
verses.17:8: If a matter for judgment is too difficult for you—between blood and blood, between lawsuit and lawsuit, and between blow and blow, matters of dispute in your gates—then you shall rise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
verses.17:9: You shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who will be in those days; you shall inquire, and they shall declare to you the word of judgment.
verses.17:10: And you shall act according to the word that they declare to you from that place which the LORD will choose, and you shall take care to do according to all that they teach you.
verses.17:11: According to the teaching that they teach you and according to the judgment that they speak to you, you shall act; you shall not turn aside from the word that they declare to you, to the right or to the left.
verses.17:12: As for the man who acts in presumption by not listening to the priest who stands to minister there to the LORD your God, or to the judge—that man shall die, and you shall purge the evil from Israel.
verses.17:13: And all the people will hear and fear, and they will not act presumptuously anymore.
