notes.2:34: "Devoted to complete destruction" translates the Hiphil of charam (the cherem ban), denoting the irreversible setting apart of a conquered population or city to the LORD for total destruction.
notes.3:8: Hebrew be-ever ha-Yarden ("beyond the Jordan") literally means "across/on the side of the Jordan" and shifts perspective within this chapter—referring to the eastern side here, and to the western side (Canaan) in 3:20 and 3:25.
notes.3:14: Havvoth-jair (Hebrew Chavvot Ya'ir) literally means "tent-villages of Jair."
notes.3:16: Hebrew tokh ha-nachal u-gevul (literally "the middle of the wadi and a border") uses an explicative waw idiomatically to define the boundary line itself, as also in "with the Jordan as a border" in 3:17.
notes.3:26: "Was furious with me" translates va-yit'abber, the Hithpael of avar II ("be furious, overflow with wrath"), forming a sharp wordplay with the homonymous Qal verb avar I ("cross over") in Moses's plea in 3:25 and God's refusal in 3:27.
notes.4:7: The Hebrew phrase for "a god so close" pairs a grammatically plural adjective with the morphologically plural noun for deity, and can be rendered either "a god so close" or "gods so close."
notes.4:13: Literally "the ten words," the Hebrew phrase traditionally referred to as the Ten Commandments.
notes.4:23: The Piel verb rendered "has forbidden you" literally means "commanded you," used elliptically in a prohibition for "commanded you not to make."
notes.4:37: The Masoretic Hebrew literally has singular suffixes, "his seed after him," functioning as a collective or distributive singular after plural "your fathers."
notes.4:48: Mount Sion reflects the Masoretic spelling Si'on, which is distinct from Jerusalem's Zion and is likely a variant of Sirion in Deuteronomy 3:9, another name for Mount Hermon.
notes.5:5: This verse forms a parenthetical aside in Hebrew interrupting 'spoke' in 5:4 and 'saying' at the end of 5:5, which introduces the LORD's words in 5:6-21.
notes.5:10: Qere reads 'My commandments,' matching first-person 'those who love Me'; ketiv writes 'His commandments' (or 'His commandment').
notes.5:17: Native Masoretic order places "You must not murder" at 5:17 (without initial waw) and "And you must not commit adultery" at 5:18 (beginning the syndetic waw chain of vv. 18–21). In the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 5:18 maps to slot 5:17 and MT 5:17 maps to slot 5:18.
notes.5:18: Native Masoretic order places "You must not murder" at 5:17 before "And you must not commit adultery" at 5:18; in the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 5:17 maps to slot 5:18 and MT 5:18 maps to slot 5:17.
notes.5:27: The second Hebrew pronoun 'you' (ve'att) is spelled and pointed in the shortened form normally used for the feminine singular, a rare Masoretic masculine usage also found in Numbers 11:15 and Ezekiel 28:14.
notes.5:29: 'If only' renders the Hebrew optative idiom mi-yitten (literally 'Who will give'), expressing an earnest wish.
notes.6:4: The verbless Hebrew confession literally reads 'the LORD our God, the LORD one,' and can also be rendered 'the LORD our God, the LORD is one' or 'the LORD is our God, the LORD alone.'
notes.6:5: 'Might' renders Hebrew me'od, ordinarily an adverb ('very' or 'exceedingly'), here used as a noun denoting one's entire strength or capacity.
notes.6:7: 'Teach them repeatedly' renders the Piel of shanan (literally 'to sharpen'), denoting diligent, repeated instruction.
notes.6:16: Hebrew contains a wordplay between 'you tested' (nissitem, Piel of nasah) and 'Massah' (hammassah, literally 'the Testing').
notes.7:4: The Hiphil verb yasir, he will turn away, has a singular subject referring back to the foreign father in 7:3, and the phrase me'acharay, from following Me, shifts abruptly into first-person divine speech before returning to third-person reference to the LORD.
notes.7:9: The form mitsvotav, His commandments, is spelled defectively without yod in the Masoretic text here and in 8:2, a traditional ketiv/qere orthographic variant whose vocalized qere reads the plural suffix.
notes.7:10: The Hebrew shifts mid-clause from plural lesone'av, those who hate Him, to distributive singular el-panav leha'avido, literally to his face to destroy him, using the idiom to his face to signify direct, personal repayment.
notes.7:13: The rare Deuteronomic phrases shegar-alafekha, the offspring of your cattle, and ashterot tso'nekha, the young of your flock, denote livestock fertility; ashterot shares an etymology with the fertility goddess Astarte but functions here purely as a term for the young of sheep and goats.
notes.7:20: The singular collective noun hatsir'ah traditionally means the hornet, as in Exodus 23:28 and Joshua 24:12, though some lexicographers understand it figuratively as panic or discouragement.
notes.8:3: The Masoretic text reads kol-motsa pi- followed by the divine name, everything that goes forth from the mouth of the LORD, without a separate noun for word as supplied in the Septuagint and later Greek citations.
notes.8:7: The plural tehomot, deep waters, derives from tehom, the deep, and denotes subterranean water sources emerging as springs across the landscape.
notes.8:8: The construct phrase zeit shemen, literally olive of oil, refers to oil-bearing olive trees rather than wild olives.
notes.8:15: The collective singular phrase nachash saraf, fiery serpents, pairs nachash, serpent, with saraf from the root meaning to burn, referring to venomous snakes whose bite burns or whose appearance is fiery.
notes.8:20: This verse pairs the Hiphil participle ma'avid, is causing to perish, with the Qal imperfect to'vedun, you will perish, from the same root avad to underscore the parallel between the fate of the dispossessed nations and a disobedient Israel.
notes.9:4: In the Masoretic Hebrew, Israel's quoted inner speech ends at "this land" (1st person "my righteousness ... brought me"), after which the adversative waw introduces Moses's correction in the 2nd person ("from before you").
notes.9:21: "Pounded it, grinding it thoroughly" reflects the Qal wayyiqtol of katat followed by two adverbial infinitives absolute: the Qal infinitive absolute of tahan ("grinding") and the Hiphil infinitive absolute of yatav ("thoroughly").
notes.9:23: "Command" translates the Hebrew idiom "mouth" (pi), referring to the LORD's spoken directive.
notes.9:28: The singular noun "the land" (ha'arets) takes a plural verb ("will say", yo'meru) by constructio ad sensum, referring by metonymy to the inhabitants of Egypt.
notes.10:4: Hebrew aseret haddevarim literally means "the Ten Words" (the Decalogue), echoing "the words" (haddevarim) in 9:10 and 10:2 and distinct from "commandments" (mitswot) in 10:13.
notes.10:6: Verses 6-7 form a brief third-person itinerary interlude before Moses's direct address to Israel resumes in verses 9-10; "served as priest" renders the Piel denominative verb from kohen ("priest").
notes.10:12: The Qal participle sho'el literally means "asking," and is answered by a chain of five lamed-infinitives construct ("to fear ... to walk ... to love ... to serve ... to observe") continuing into verse 13.
notes.10:17: "Shows no partiality" translates the Hebrew idiom lo'-yissa' fanim, literally "does not lift up faces," meaning not favoring one party over another in judgment.
notes.11:2: The parenthetical Hebrew clause "for not with your children" (ki lo et-beneikhem) is elliptical, lacking an explicit verb; "I am not addressing" is supplied for clarity, while the accusative series in verses 2-6 is governed by "know" and resumed in verse 7.
notes.11:6: "At their feet" (be-ragleihem) is a Hebrew idiom meaning "in their train" or "following them," referring to the people and animals belonging to the company of Dathan and Abiram.
notes.11:13: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts into first-person divine speech in verses 13-15 ("My commandments ... I will give"), with Moses speaking directly in the voice of the LORD before returning to third-person reference to the LORD in verse 17.
notes.11:27: The relative particle asher here carries conditional force ("if"), standing directly parallel to im ("if") in verse 28.
notes.12:5: The noun rendered "His dwelling place" (shikhno, from shakhan, "to dwell") occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; the Masoretic accentuation pairs it directly with "you shall seek."
notes.12:12: "Within your gates" is a recurring Deuteronomic idiom (also vv. 15, 17, 18, 21) denoting "in your towns" or "within your local settlements."
notes.12:22: The Niphal passive verb ye'akhel ("is eaten") governs direct-object markers before its logical subjects ("the gazelle and the deer"), a classic impersonal passive construction in Biblical Hebrew (literally "as one eats the gazelle and the deer").
notes.12:30: "Ensnared into following them" renders a pregnant Hebrew construction (tinnaqesh achareihem, Niphal of naqash, literally "be ensnared after them").
notes.13:1: The Masoretic Text begins chapter 13 with this verse; in the verse division of the Latin Vulgate tradition it is 12:32, and the remaining verses of chapter 13 are numbered one lower there.
notes.13:6: The Hiphil of nadach (literally "thrust/drive away") is used consistently in vv. 6, 11, and 14 for driving or leading someone astray from faithfulness to the LORD. Here sarah ("rebellion") literally denotes turning aside or defection.
notes.13:14: Hebrew anashim bene-beliyya'al is literally "men, sons of worthlessness" (or "wickedness"). The same noun beliyya'al recurs in 15:9 for a "worthless" thought.
notes.13:16: The Hiphil infinitive absolute hacharem ("devoting to destruction," from charam) denotes placing persons or property under the irreversible ban (cherem, v. 18) dedicated to the LORD. In v. 17, kalil ("whole offering") is a sacrificial term for an offering consumed entirely by fire.
notes.14:5: The exact zoological identifications of several wild ruminants in this list—especially yachmur ("fallow deer"), aqqo ("wild goat"), dishon ("addax"), teo ("oryx"), and zamer ("mountain sheep")—remain uncertain.
notes.14:8: Hebrew velo gerah is elliptical (literally "and not cud"), omitting the participle for chewing/bringing up the cud from v. 7.
notes.14:13: The Masoretic Text lists three birds here (ra'ah, ayyah, and dayyah), whereas the parallel list in Leviticus 11:14 has two (da'ah and ayyah); exact species identifications for many of the unclean birds in vv. 12-18 are uncertain.
notes.14:21: Hebrew nevelah refers specifically to the carcass of an animal that died naturally rather than by slaughter (compare "their carcasses" in v. 8). The Qal infinitive absolute makhor ("sell") functions permissively alongside the finite verb tittenennah ("you may give it").
notes.15:2: The Qal infinitive absolute shamot ("release") functions jussively, followed by kol-ba'al mashsheh yado, literally "every holder of a loan of his hand" (that is, every creditor). In the final clause, the indefinite third-person verb qara ("one has proclaimed") is rendered passively ("has been proclaimed").
notes.15:6: Hebrew contrasts two stems of the same verb avat ("give or take a pledge"): the Hiphil veha'avatta ("you will lend") and the Qal lo ta'avot ("you will not borrow"), with the Hiphil recurring in v. 8.
notes.15:9: Hebrew vera'ah enekha (literally "and your eye is evil") is an idiom for stinginess or hostility; the same Qal verb ra'a ("be evil/begrudging") recurs in v. 10 with the heart (lo-yera levavekha).
notes.15:14: The Hiphil infinitive absolute and imperfect ha'aneq ta'aniq ("supply generously") derive from anaq ("necklace"), occurring in the Hiphil only here in the Hebrew Bible with the sense of adorning or loading someone generously with provisions.
notes.15:18: Hebrew mishneh sekhar sakhir literally means "double the wages of a hired worker," indicating that six years of continuous bondservice yielded twice the value of hiring a laborer (some interpret mishneh here as "equivalent to").
notes.16:5: Hebrew she'arekha ("your gates") is used metonymically throughout Deuteronomy for Israel's walled towns and settlements (compare 16:11, 14, 18; 17:2, 8; 18:6).
notes.16:7: The Piel verb bishalta (from bashal) commonly denotes boiling or cooking more broadly, rendered here generally as "cook."
notes.16:10: Hebrew missat ("the measure of") is a hapax legomenon occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible, denoting sufficiency, measure, or proportion (cognate with Aramaic missat, "enough").
notes.16:16: The Masoretic text vocalizes yera'eh as a Niphal ("be seen / appear") followed by the direct-object marker et-pene ("the face of"), a recurring festival idiom that some grammarians view as a reverential vocalization of an original Qal ("see the face of").
notes.16:20: Hebrew repeats the noun (tsedeq tsedeq, "justice, justice") for emphatic intensity and exclusivity, conveying "justice and nothing but justice."
notes.17:3: The text shifts abruptly to first-person divine speech (lo-tsivviti, Piel perfect of tsavah, "which I have not commanded") without a quotation formula.
notes.17:8: The three paired expressions cover difficult judicial distinctions involving homicide ("blood and blood," dam), civil or legal claims ("lawsuit and lawsuit," din), and physical assault or skin affliction ("blow and blow," nega').
notes.17:9: "The Levitical priests" translates the characteristic Deuteronomic appositional phrase ha-kohanim ha-leviyyim, literally "the priests, the Levites" (compare 17:18; 18:1).
notes.17:18: Hebrew mishneh ha-torah ha-zot means "a copy/duplicate of this law" (rendered in the Septuagint as to deuteronomion touto, "this second law," whence the English name Deuteronomy). The compound preposition millifne ("from before") indicates copying from the authoritative scroll kept by the Levitical priests.
notes.18:1: "His inheritance" (ve-nachalato) refers to the sacred dues, offerings, and portions belonging to the LORD that are allotted to the tribe of Levi for sustenance.
notes.18:8: Hebrew levad mimkarav al-ha'avot literally reads "apart from his sales upon/concerning the fathers," a compressed legal phrase referring to personal proceeds from the sale of patrimonial holdings.
notes.18:10: Verses 10-11 use technical participial forms for forbidden occult practices, including me'onen (Polel participle, "soothsayer/augur"), menachesh (Piel participle, "omen reader"), chover chaver ("binder/caster of spells"), and sho'el ov ve-yid'oni ("inquirer of a ghost/medium or familiar spirit").
notes.18:22: "You shall not dread him" translates the Qal imperfect lo tagur mimmennu (from gur II, "stand in dread/awe of"), a stronger term for fearful deference than the more general yare' ("fear").
notes.19:4: Literally "without knowledge" and "from yesterday and the third day," standard Hebrew idioms for acting accidentally and having no prior hostility.
notes.19:10: Hebrew damim (plural of dam, "blood") denotes culpability for shed blood, appearing here with a singular verb.
notes.19:16: "Malicious witness" is literally "a witness of violence," referring to one who gives false testimony to inflict unjust harm.
notes.20:6: The Piel verb hillel (literally "make common") refers to releasing the produce of a new vineyard for ordinary consumption after its initial consecrated period (cf. Lev 19:23-25).
notes.20:8: The Masoretic verb yimmas is Niphal ("melt") followed by the direct object marker et before "the heart of his brothers," an unusual construction where et introduces the subject of a passive/intransitive verb (or else the verb is read causatively, "he will not make the heart of his brothers melt").
notes.20:19: Although ha-adam is pointed with the definite article rather than an interrogative prefix, the clause is widely understood as an unmarked rhetorical question (literally "For is the human being a tree of the field, to come from before you into the siege?").
notes.21:7: Translating the Masoretic qere shafekhu (3rd-person common plural, matching dual "our hands"); the ketiv shafekhah has a feminine singular or archaic feminine plural ending.
notes.21:8: "Shall be atoned for" renders a rare Nithpael (hybrid Niphal-Hithpael passive-reflexive) form of kafar ("atone").
notes.21:12: "Trim her nails" is literally "do" or "tend her nails"; the idiom usually means paring the nails (cf. 2 Sam 19:24), though some ancient interpreters understood it as letting them grow as a sign of mourning.
notes.21:14: The rare Hithpael verb hit-ammer (occurring only here and Deut 24:7) denotes treating someone harshly, exploiting them, or dealing with them as a slave.
notes.21:23: The Hebrew construct "a curse of God" (qillelat elohim) may be understood either as a subjective genitive ("cursed by God") or as an objective genitive ("an affront to God").
notes.22:5: Hebrew keli-gever ('an article/equipment of a man') is broader than simlah ('garment') in the second clause and can encompass male attire, accessories, or gear.
notes.22:9: Hebrew tiqdash (Qal imperfect of qadash) literally means 'will become holy/consecrated,' referring to produce forfeited to the sanctuary and thus forbidden for ordinary use.
notes.22:11: Hebrew shaatnez is a technical term for mixed-fiber fabric, immediately defined here as wool and linen combined together.
notes.22:14: Hebrew alilot devarim (lit. 'pretexts/deeds of words,' recurring in v. 17) denotes trumped-up or baseless accusations.
notes.22:15: Here and in vv. 16, 20-21, and 23-29 (unlike v. 19), the consonantal text writes the archaic Pentateuchal form naar without final he, vocalized as a qere perpetuum for feminine naarah ('young woman').
notes.23:1: Hebrew kenaph aviv literally means 'the wing/corner of his father,' referring to the corner of a garment or covering as an idiom for marital rights and intimacy (cf. Ruth 3:9).
notes.23:3: Hebrew mamzer (occurring only here and in Zech 9:6) denotes someone born of an illicit or forbidden union; its exact legal scope is debated.
notes.23:5: Hebrew sakhar ('he hired') is singular, referring specifically to Moab, though rendered 'they hired' to agree with the plural verb earlier in the verse. Aram-naharaim literally means 'Aram of the Two Rivers,' i.e., Upper Mesopotamia.
notes.23:14: Hebrew azenekha ('your equipment/gear') is a hapax legomenon whose exact sense is uncertain, commonly understood as personal tools, weapons, or field gear.
notes.23:18: Hebrew qedeshah (fem.) and qadesh (masc.) literally mean 'consecrated woman' and 'consecrated man,' referring to cultic personnel associated with illicit sexual rites, paired with 'prostitute' and 'dog' (likely a contemptuous metaphor for a male prostitute) in v. 19.
notes.23:26: Native Masoretic order places the vineyard law at 23:25 and the standing-grain law at 23:26 (corresponding to 23:24–25 in alternative versifications); in the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 23:25 maps to slot 23:26 and MT 23:26 maps to slot 23:25.
notes.24:1: Hebrew erwat dabar literally means "nakedness of a matter," an idiom denoting something indecent or improper. Verses 1-3 form a single extended conditional protasis whose legal prohibition appears in verse 4.
notes.24:4: The verb rendered "has been defiled" is the rare Hothpaal passive-reflexive perfect of the root meaning to be unclean, emphasizing that the woman is regarded as defiled with respect to her first husband.
notes.24:7: The Hithpael verb hit'ammer, occurring only here and in Deuteronomy 21:14, denotes treating a captive brutally, tyrannically, or as a slave.
notes.24:20: The Piel verb tefa'er is a denominative from po'rah, meaning "bough" or "branch," and denotes going back through the olive branches a second time.
notes.25:2: Hebrew bin hakkot literally means "a son of striking," using the Hiphil infinitive construct of the verb to strike as an idiom for deserving a beating.
notes.25:5: The Piel verb yibbem, appearing here and in verse 7, is a denominative from yabam, "husband's brother," denoting the levirate duty of marrying a deceased brother's childless widow to preserve his line.
notes.25:13: Hebrew eben wa'aben, literally "a stone and a stone," and efah we'efah in verse 14, literally "an ephah and an ephah," use repetition to denote dishonest dual standards for scale weights and dry grain measures.
notes.25:18: The Piel verb wayzanneb is a denominative from zanab, "tail," meaning to cut off the rear of a marching column; hanneheshalim is a Niphal participle occurring only here in Biblical Hebrew, denoting those who are feeble or lagging behind.
notes.26:5: Hebrew arammi obed uses the Qal active participle of the verb meaning to perish or be lost, literally "a perishing Aramean," also widely understood as "a wandering Aramean" referring to Jacob's vulnerable nomadic state or famine-driven descent into Egypt.
notes.26:12: The form la'ser is a syncopated Hiphil infinitive construct of the verb meaning to tithe, denoting the formal setting aside or delivery of the third-year tithe.
notes.26:14: Hebrew be'oni, "during my mourning," derives from a noun meaning sorrow or mourning as in Hosea 9:4, a state that rendered consecrated food ritually unfit to eat.
notes.26:17: The Hiphil of the verb meaning "to say," he'emarta here and he'emireka in verse 18, occurs only in these two verses in the Hebrew Bible, expressing a solemn mutual covenantal affirmation or eliciting of a pledge between Israel and the LORD.
notes.27:4: The Masoretic Text reads "on Mount Ebal," whereas the Samaritan Pentateuch reads "on Mount Gerizim."
notes.27:8: "clearly and thoroughly" renders two adverbial infinitives absolute: the Piel infinitive absolute of ba'ar ("make plain/clear") and the Hiphil infinitive absolute of yatav ("do well/thoroughly").
notes.27:9: "Keep silent" renders the Hiphil imperative of sakat, a word occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible, calling for hushed attention.
notes.27:20: "uncovered the edge of his father's garment" renders a Hebrew idiom (literally "uncovered his father's wing/hem," cf. Deut 23:1) denoting the violation of his father's marital bed.
notes.27:26: The Masoretic Text reads "the words of this law" without "all" (contrast vv. 3 and 8), whereas the Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint include "all."
notes.28:22: The Masoretic vocalization reads cherev ('sword'); an alternate vocalization of the same consonants, chorev, means 'drought,' which aligns with the surrounding climatic and crop afflictions.
notes.28:25: After plural 'your enemies,' the Hebrew shifts to collective masculine singular suffixes (literally 'against him ... before him'), rendered 'them' for English agreement.
notes.28:27: The ketiv reads ba'ophalim ('with swellings' or 'with tumors'); the Masoretic qere substitutes the euphemistic battechorim ('with hemorrhoids'), followed in the translation.
notes.28:30: The ketiv reads yishgalennah ('will violate/ravish her'); the Masoretic qere substitutes the euphemistic yishkavennah ('will lie with her'), followed here. In the final clause, the Piel verb chalal literally means 'make common' or 'deconsecrate,' referring to harvesting a new vineyard's fruit for ordinary use (cf. Lev 19:23-25; Deut 20:6).
notes.28:32: The clause 'there will be no power in your hand' renders the Hebrew idiom 'ein le'el yadekha (literally 'there is not in the strength of your hand'), expressing complete helplessness.
notes.28:42: 'The cricket' translates the rare noun tselatsal, derived from a root meaning 'to buzz' or 'whirr,' referring to a buzzing locust or cricket; yeyaresh is the sole Piel occurrence of yarash ('possess, take over') in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.28:48: After plural 'your enemies,' Hebrew uses a collective masculine singular suffix on yeshallechennu (literally 'whom the LORD will send him'). The subject of 'He will place ... until He destroys' is the LORD.
notes.28:54: 'His eye will turn begrudging' renders the Hebrew idiom tera' 'eino (literally 'his eye will be evil toward,' repeated in v. 56), denoting extreme stinginess and hostility.
notes.28:66: 'Will hang in suspense' translates telu'im (Qal passive participle of tala', a by-form of talah, 'hang'), portraying life as hanging precariously in constant uncertainty.
notes.28:68: 'You will put yourselves up for sale' translates the Hithpael hitmakkartem (conative reflexive of makar, 'sell'), vividly depicting desperate self-enslavement that fails because no one will buy.
notes.29:4: Here and in v. 5 ("I led you... I am the LORD your God"), Moses shifts abruptly from third-person reference to the LORD (vv. 1-3) into first-person divine speech before returning to first-person plural with Israel ("us... we") in v. 6.
notes.29:8: "succeed" translates the Hiphil of sakal, which encompasses both acting wisely and achieving success as the fruit of wisdom.
notes.29:9: The Masoretic text attaches the second-person plural suffix to both nouns (rashekem shivtekem, "your heads, your tribes"), either listing them in series or placing "your tribes" in apposition to "your heads" (unlike the construct reading "heads of your tribes" in the Septuagint and Samaritan Pentateuch).
notes.29:18: "so as to sweep away the watered with the dry" renders the Qal infinitive construct of saphah with two feminine adjectives (haravah and hatsemeah), probably a merism for total devastation; Hebrew alah ("sworn curse" here and in vv. 19-20, 30:7) denotes a covenant oath backed by imprecations (rendered "oath" in vv. 11, 13).
notes.29:28: In the Masoretic text, extraordinary dots (puncta extraordinaria) mark the ten letters of lanu ulevanenu ("to us and to our children") and the first letter (ayin) of ad ("forever"), an ancient scribal marking whose original significance is debated.
notes.30:3: "restore your fortunes" renders the Hebrew idiom shuv shevut (Qal of shuv with the cognate noun shevut), meaning to reverse a condition and restore former well-being, while playing acoustically on captivity (root shavah) in exilic contexts.
notes.30:11: "not beyond you" translates the Niphal participle of pala with the preposition min ("too extraordinary/difficult for you"), denoting what exceeds human grasp or capability.
notes.30:16: The Masoretic text begins directly with the conjunction asher ("in that") linking to v. 15, without the longer conditional clause ("If you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God") found in the Septuagint.
notes.30:18: "certainly perish" renders the emphatic Qal infinitive absolute paired with the Qal imperfect of avad (avod tovedun), underscoring the certainty of destruction.
notes.31:6: The Hiphil verb from rph literally means 'let go of' or 'drop', paired with Qal azav ('abandon'), the same verb that recurs in verses 8, 16, and 17.
notes.31:7: MT reads Qal imperfect tavo ('you will go') with the preposition et ('with'), contrasting with verse 23, which uses Hiphil tavi ('you will bring') with the direct object marker et.
notes.31:11: MT points the infinitive construct as Niphal leraot ('to appear'), with et-pene functioning adverbially as 'in the presence of' or 'before'.
notes.31:19: The Hebrew imperatives shift from second-person masculine plural ('write ... for yourselves', addressing both Moses and Joshua) to second-person masculine singular (Piel 'teach it' and Qal 'place it', addressing Moses).
notes.31:23: MT supplies no explicit subject noun for the verb 'commissioned'; the first-person divine promises ('I swore ... I Myself will be with you') and the fulfillment of verse 14 identify the speaker as the LORD.
notes.32:5: The Masoretic syntax is condensed and difficult, literally reading "acted corruptly toward Him, not His children, their blemish," with the singular Piel verb שִׁחֵת referring to Israel collectively.
notes.32:8: The Masoretic Text reads "the sons of Israel" (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), whereas a Dead Sea Scroll manuscript (4QDeutj) reads "sons of God" and the Septuagint reads "angels of God."
notes.32:13: Ketiv במותי and qere בָּמֳתֵי represent an orthographic variant in the construct plural of בָּמָה ("heights" or "high places"), with the qere omitting the vav; both carry the same meaning.
notes.32:26: The hapax verb אַפְאֵיהֶם (Hiphil imperfect 1cs of פאה with 3mp suffix) is understood either as "cleave them in pieces" or, denominatively from פֵּאָה ("corner, edge"), as "scatter them to the corners."
notes.32:28: Hebrew has no quotation marks; closing the quotation at v. 27 reflects the shift from first-person divine speech (vv. 20–27) to third-person reflection and first-person plural ("our Rock," v. 31), though some interpreters extend the LORD's speech through v. 29 or v. 33. The referent of "they" across vv. 28–33 (Israel vs. Israel's enemies) is likewise debated.
notes.32:34: Hebrew introduces no new speech formula here, though the abrupt return to first-person singular pronouns ("with Me," "My storehouses," "Mine" in vv. 34–35) marks a resumption of divine speech before third-person narration returns in v. 36.
notes.32:43: In the Masoretic Text, the Hiphil imperative הַרְנִינוּ takes עַמּוֹ ("His people") directly without a preposition ("Acclaim His people, nations"), and אַדְמָתוֹ עַמּוֹ ("His land, His people") is asyndetic; 4QDeutq and the Septuagint preserve longer texts with additional lines.
notes.33:2: Ketiv/Qere: the ketiv is written as one word (אשדת, often taken as "fiery slopes" or "flashing fire"), while the qere divides it into two words (אֵשׁ דָּת, "fire of law," i.e., "a fiery law"), which is translated here. Also, "myriads of holy ones" renders מֵרִבְבֹת קֹדֶשׁ (literally "from myriads of holiness").
notes.33:3: The verb תֻּכּוּ is a hapax legomenon (usually parsed as a Pual perfect of an uncertain root תכה), understood as "settled down" or "followed closely" at Your feet. The following verb יִשָּׂא is third-person masculine singular, used distributively ("each one receives").
notes.33:6: Literally the second clause reads "and let his men be a number" (מִסְפָּר, idiomatically "few in number"); the negative particle אַל ("not") from the preceding jussive is understood to carry over by poetic ellipsis, though some read it concessively ("though his men be few").
notes.33:12: The antecedents of the third-person masculine singular pronouns in the final clause (וּבֵין כְּתֵפָיו שָׁכֵן) are ambiguous: either the LORD dwells between Benjamin's shoulders (evoking the slopes/ridges of Benjamin's territory), as rendered here, or Benjamin dwells securely between the LORD's shoulders.
notes.33:25: Both מִנְעָלֶךָ ("your bolts," from נעל "to lock/bolt," though anciently also understood as "your sandals") and דׇּבְאֶךָ (understood as "your strength," or by some comparative Semitic scholars "your security/rest") are hapax legomena in Biblical Hebrew.
notes.34:5: "At the LORD's command" translates the Hebrew idiom עַל־פִּי יְהֹוָה, literally "by the mouth of the LORD."
notes.34:6: The verb וַיִּקְבֹּר is a third-person masculine singular active Qal wayyiqtol ("and He buried him"), with the LORD as the understood subject, though it is sometimes interpreted impersonally ("he was buried").
notes.34:7: The noun לֵחֹה ("his vitality," from לֵחַ, literally "moisture" or "freshness") is a hapax legomenon with the archaic third-person masculine singular suffix -ֹה, and the verb נָס literally means "fled."

native_verses.1:1: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel on the other side of the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah facing Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
native_verses.1:2: It is eleven days from Horeb, by the way of Mount Seir, as far as Kadesh-barnea.
native_verses.1:3: Now it happened in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first of the month, that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel according to all that the LORD had commanded him regarding them,
native_verses.1:4: after he had struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
native_verses.1:5: On the other side of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses resolved to explain this law, saying:
native_verses.1:6: The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, "You have stayed at this mountain long enough.
native_verses.1:7: Turn and set out, and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Negev, and by the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates River.
native_verses.1:8: Look, I have put the land before you. Go in and possess the land that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them."
native_verses.1:9: Then I spoke to you at that time, saying, "I am unable to bear you alone.
native_verses.1:10: The LORD your God has multiplied you, and here you are today, like the stars of the heavens in multitude.
native_verses.1:11: May the LORD, the God of your fathers, add to you a thousand times as many as you are and bless you, just as He has spoken to you!
native_verses.1:12: How can I bear by myself your trouble, your burden, and your disputes?
native_verses.1:13: Bring forward for yourselves wise, discerning, and well-known men for your tribes, and I will set them as your heads."
native_verses.1:14: Then you answered me and said, "The thing you have spoken is good to do."
native_verses.1:15: So I took the heads of your tribes, men who were wise and well-known, and made them heads over you: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes.
native_verses.1:16: And I commanded your judges at that time, saying, "Hear disputes between your brothers and judge with righteousness between a man and his brother or the resident alien with him.
native_verses.1:17: You shall not show favoritism in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great equally. You shall not dread any man, for judgment belongs to God. And the matter that is too difficult for you, you shall bring before me, and I will hear it."
native_verses.1:18: And at that time I commanded you all the things that you were to do.
native_verses.1:19: Then we set out from Horeb and walked through all that great and fearsome wilderness you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, just as the LORD our God commanded us, and we came as far as Kadesh-barnea.
native_verses.1:20: Then I said to you, "You have come as far as the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving to us.
native_verses.1:21: Look, the LORD your God has put the land before you. Go up, possess it, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has spoken to you. Do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed."
native_verses.1:22: Then all of you drew near to me and said, "Let us send men ahead of us so that they may explore the land for us and bring word back to us about the way by which we should go up and the cities to which we will come."
native_verses.1:23: The matter seemed good in my eyes, so I took twelve men from you, one man for each tribe.
native_verses.1:24: They turned and went up into the hill country, came as far as the Valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.
native_verses.1:25: They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and they brought word back to us and said, "The land that the LORD our God is giving to us is good."
native_verses.1:26: Yet you were unwilling to go up, and you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
native_verses.1:27: You grumbled in your tents and said, "Because the LORD hates us, He brought us out from the land of Egypt to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.
native_verses.1:28: Where are we going up? Our brothers have caused our hearts to melt, saying, 'The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified up to the heavens; and moreover we saw sons of the Anakim there.'"
native_verses.1:29: And I said to you, "Do not be terrified and do not be afraid of them.
native_verses.1:30: The LORD your God, who goes before you, He Himself will fight for you, according to all that He did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
native_verses.1:31: and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, just as a man carries his son, along the entire way you walked until you reached this place."
native_verses.1:32: Yet despite this word, you did not trust in the LORD your God,
native_verses.1:33: who went before you along the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way in which you should walk, and in the cloud by day.
native_verses.1:34: And the LORD heard the sound of your words; He grew angry and swore, saying,
native_verses.1:35: "Not a man among these men, this evil generation, shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers,
native_verses.1:36: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him I will give the land on which he trod, and to his sons, because he followed the LORD completely."
native_verses.1:37: Even with me the LORD grew angry because of you, saying, "You too shall not enter there.
native_verses.1:38: Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall enter there. Strengthen him, for he will give it to Israel as an inheritance.
native_verses.1:39: And your little ones, who you said would become plunder, and your children, who today do not know good and evil, they shall enter there, and to them I will give it, and they shall possess it.
native_verses.1:40: But you, turn back and set out into the wilderness along the way of the Sea of Reeds."
native_verses.1:41: Then you answered and said to me, "We have sinned against the LORD. We ourselves will go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us." Then each of you strapped on his weapons of war, and you considered it a light thing to go up into the hill country.
native_verses.1:42: And the LORD said to me, "Say to them, 'Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not in your midst, so that you will not be struck down before your enemies.'"
native_verses.1:43: So I spoke to you, yet you did not listen; you rebelled against the command of the LORD, and you acted arrogantly and went up into the hill country.
native_verses.1:44: Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and pursued you just as bees do, and they crushed you in Seir as far as Hormah.
native_verses.1:45: Then you came back and wept before the LORD, yet the LORD did not listen to your voice, nor did He pay attention to you.
native_verses.1:46: So you stayed at Kadesh many days, for as many days as you stayed.
native_verses.2:1: Then we turned and traveled toward the wilderness along the road to the Sea of Reeds, just as the LORD had spoken to me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.
native_verses.2:2: Then the LORD said to me:
native_verses.2:3: "You have gone around this mountain long enough; turn yourselves northward.
native_verses.2:4: And command the people, saying, 'You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir. They will fear you, so guard yourselves very closely.
native_verses.2:5: Do not engage them in conflict, for I will not give you any of their land—not even a stepping place for the sole of a foot—because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.
native_verses.2:6: You shall buy food from them with silver and eat, and you shall also purchase water from them with silver and drink.
native_verses.2:7: For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand; He has known your walking through this great wilderness. Throughout these forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have not lacked anything.'"
native_verses.2:8: So we passed on from our brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the Arabah road, from Elath and from Ezion-geber; then we turned and passed along the road to the wilderness of Moab.
native_verses.2:9: Then the LORD said to me, "Do not show hostility toward Moab, and do not engage them in battle, for I will not give you any of its land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as a possession."
native_verses.2:10: The Emim lived in it formerly, a people great and numerous and tall like the Anakim.
native_verses.2:11: They too are reckoned as Rephaim, like the Anakim, though the Moabites call them Emim.
native_verses.2:12: And in Seir the Horites lived formerly, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them, and destroyed them from before themselves, and lived in their place, just as Israel did to the land of its possession that the LORD gave to them.
native_verses.2:13: "Now rise up and cross the Wadi Zered for yourselves." So we crossed the Wadi Zered.
native_verses.2:14: And the days that we traveled from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Wadi Zered totaled thirty-eight years, until the entire generation—the men of war—had perished from the midst of the camp, just as the LORD had sworn to them.
native_verses.2:15: Moreover, the hand of the LORD was against them to rout them from the midst of the camp until they perished.
native_verses.2:16: So it happened, when all the men of war had finished dying from the midst of the people,
native_verses.2:17: that the LORD spoke to me, saying:
native_verses.2:18: "This day you are crossing the border of Moab, at Ar.
native_verses.2:19: When you draw near opposite the sons of Ammon, do not show hostility toward them and do not engage them in conflict, for I will not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as a possession."
native_verses.2:20: It too is reckoned as a land of Rephaim; Rephaim lived in it formerly, though the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
native_verses.2:21: a people great and numerous and tall like the Anakim. Yet the LORD destroyed them from before them, and they dispossessed them and lived in their place,
native_verses.2:22: just as He did for the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites from before them, and they dispossessed them and have lived in their place until this day.
native_verses.2:23: And as for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who came out from Caphtor, destroyed them and lived in their place.
native_verses.2:24: "Rise up, set out, and cross the Wadi Arnon! Look, I have given into your hand Sihon king of Heshbon, the Amorite, and his land. Begin to take possession, and engage him in battle.
native_verses.2:25: This day I will begin to place the dread of you and the fear of you upon the peoples beneath all the heavens, who will hear the report of you and will quake and writhe before you."
native_verses.2:26: Then I dispatched messengers from the Wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with words of peace, saying:
native_verses.2:27: "Let me pass through your land. I will walk strictly along the road; I will not turn aside right or left.
native_verses.2:28: Sell me food for silver and I will eat, and give me water for silver and I will drink—just let me pass through on foot,
native_verses.2:29: just as the sons of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving to us."
native_verses.2:30: Yet Sihon, king of Heshbon, was not willing to let us pass by him, for the LORD your God made his spirit stiff and made his heart stubborn, so as to give him into your hand, as it is this day.
native_verses.2:31: Then the LORD said to me, "Look, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over before you. Begin—take possession, to possess his land."
native_verses.2:32: Then Sihon came out to meet us—he and all his people—for battle at Jahaz.
native_verses.2:33: And the LORD our God gave him over before us, and we struck down him and his sons and all his people.
native_verses.2:34: So we captured all his cities at that time and devoted to complete destruction every city—men, women, and little ones; we left no survivor.
native_verses.2:35: Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, together with the spoil of the cities that we captured.
native_verses.2:36: From Aroer, which is on the rim of the Wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the wadi, all the way to Gilead, there was not a town that stood too high for us; the LORD our God gave all of it over before us.
native_verses.2:37: Only to the land of the sons of Ammon you did not draw near—all along the side of the Wadi Jabbok, and the cities of the hill country, and all that the LORD our God had commanded.
native_verses.3:1: Then we turned and went up along the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came out to meet us—he and all his people—for battle at Edrei.
native_verses.3:2: Then the LORD said to me, "Do not be afraid of him, for into your hand I have given him, along with all his people and his land; and you shall do to him just as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
native_verses.3:3: So the LORD our God also gave into our hand Og, king of Bashan, and all his people, and we struck him down until no survivor was left to him.
native_verses.3:4: And we captured all his cities at that time; there was not a town that we did not take from them—sixty cities, the entire district of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
native_verses.3:5: All these were fortified cities with high walls, double gates, and bars, apart from very many unwalled cities.
native_verses.3:6: And we devoted them to complete destruction, just as we had done to Sihon, king of Heshbon, devoting to complete destruction every city—men, women, and little ones.
native_verses.3:7: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
native_verses.3:8: So at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon.
native_verses.3:9: The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir.
native_verses.3:10: All the cities of the tableland, along with all Gilead and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei—the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
native_verses.3:11: For only Og, king of Bashan, was left from the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bed was a bed of iron—is it not in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon? Nine cubits is its length and four cubits its width, by a man's cubit.
native_verses.3:12: So we took possession of this land at that time: from Aroer, which is beside the Wadi Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
native_verses.3:13: And the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh—the entire district of Argob, with all Bashan; that is called the land of Rephaim.
native_verses.3:14: Jair the son of Manasseh took the entire district of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and named them—that is, Bashan—after his own name, Havvoth-jair, until this day.
native_verses.3:15: And I gave Gilead to Machir.
native_verses.3:16: And to the Reubenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gilead even to the Wadi Arnon—the middle of the wadi as a border—and as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon,
native_verses.3:17: as well as the Arabah, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth even to the Sea of the Arabah—the Salt Sea—below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
native_verses.3:18: Then I commanded you at that time, saying, "The LORD your God has given you this land to possess it. You shall cross over armed for battle ahead of your brothers, the sons of Israel—all the men of valor.
native_verses.3:19: Only your wives, your little ones, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—shall remain in your cities that I have given to you,
native_verses.3:20: until the LORD gives rest to your brothers, just as to you, and they too take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving to them beyond the Jordan. Then you shall return, each man to his possession that I have given to you."
native_verses.3:21: And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, "Your own eyes have seen everything that the LORD your God did to these two kings; thus the LORD will do to all the kingdoms where you are crossing over.
native_verses.3:22: You must not fear them, for the LORD your God—He is the one who fights for you."
native_verses.3:23: Then I implored the LORD at that time, saying:
native_verses.3:24: "Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand; for what god is there in the heavens or on the earth who can do anything like Your works and Your mighty deeds?
native_verses.3:25: Please let me cross over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon."
native_verses.3:26: Yet the LORD was furious with me on your account and did not listen to me. And the LORD said to me, "Enough for you! Do not speak to Me any further about this matter.
native_verses.3:27: Go up to the summit of Pisgah and lift your eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, and see with your own eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.
native_verses.3:28: And command Joshua, strengthen him, and encourage him, for he will cross over ahead of this people, and he will cause them to inherit the land that you will see."
native_verses.3:29: And we stayed in the valley facing Beth-peor.
native_verses.4:1: And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the judgments that I am teaching you to carry out, so that you may live and enter and possess the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving to you.
native_verses.4:2: You must not add to the word that I am commanding you, and you must not subtract from it, in order to keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I am commanding you.
native_verses.4:3: Your very eyes saw what the LORD did at Baal-peor, for every man who walked after Baal-peor, the LORD your God wiped him out from your midst.
native_verses.4:4: Yet you who cling to the LORD your God, all of you are alive today.
native_verses.4:5: Look, I have taught you statutes and judgments, just as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you do so in the midst of the land that you are entering to possess.
native_verses.4:6: Keep them and carry them out, for this is your wisdom and your discernment in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, "Truly, a wise and discerning people is this great nation."
native_verses.4:7: For what great nation is there that has a god so close to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to Him?
native_verses.4:8: And what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments as righteous as all this law that I am placing before you today?
native_verses.4:9: Only watch yourself and guard your soul very carefully, so that you do not forget the things your eyes saw and so that they do not depart from your heart all the days of your life; and make them known to your children and to your children's children—
native_verses.4:10: the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, "Assemble the people to Me, and I will let them hear My words, so that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live on the earth, and that they may teach their children."
native_verses.4:11: Then you drew near and stood at the foot of the mountain, while the mountain was burning with fire up to the heart of the heavens—darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
native_verses.4:12: And the LORD spoke to you from within the fire. You were hearing the sound of words, yet you were seeing no form—only a voice.
native_verses.4:13: He declared to you His covenant that He commanded you to carry out—the ten words—and He wrote them on two stone tablets.
native_verses.4:14: And at that time the LORD commanded me to teach you statutes and judgments, for you to carry them out in the land that you are crossing over to possess.
native_verses.4:15: So watch very carefully over your souls, since you did not see any form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from within the fire,
native_verses.4:16: so that you do not act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, the form of any statue, the figure of male or female,
native_verses.4:17: the figure of any animal that is on the earth, the figure of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
native_verses.4:18: the figure of anything creeping on the ground, the figure of any fish that is in the waters below the earth;
native_verses.4:19: and so that you do not lift your eyes toward the heavens and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens, and be led astray and bow down to them and serve them—those that the LORD your God has apportioned to all the peoples beneath all the heavens.
native_verses.4:20: But the LORD took you and brought you out from the iron furnace, from Egypt, to become a people of inheritance for Him, as on this day.
native_verses.4:21: Now the LORD grew angry with me on account of you, and He swore that I would not cross over the Jordan and would not go into the good land that the LORD your God is giving to you as an inheritance.
native_verses.4:22: For I am going to die in this land; I am not crossing over the Jordan. Yet you are crossing over and will possess this good land.
native_verses.4:23: Be on guard for yourselves, so that you do not forget the covenant of the LORD your God that He made with you and make for yourselves a carved image—a form of anything the LORD your God has forbidden you.
native_verses.4:24: For the LORD your God—He is a devouring fire, a jealous God.
native_verses.4:25: When you have children and children's children and grow old in the land, and act corruptly and make a carved image—a form of anything—and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God to provoke Him to anger,
native_verses.4:26: I summon the heavens and the earth to witness against you today that you will surely perish swiftly from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not prolong your days on it, for you will certainly be wiped out.
native_verses.4:27: And the LORD will disperse you among the peoples, and you will remain few in number among the nations where the LORD will drive you.
native_verses.4:28: And there you will serve gods, the work of human hands—wood and stone—that do not see and do not hear and do not eat and do not smell.
native_verses.4:29: Yet from there you will seek the LORD your God and find Him, when you search for Him with your whole heart and with your whole soul.
native_verses.4:30: In your distress, when all these things find you in the latter days, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice.
native_verses.4:31: For the LORD your God is a compassionate God; He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant of your fathers that He swore to them.
native_verses.4:32: For inquire now about earlier days that were before you, since the day God created mankind on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: has anything like this great thing ever occurred, or has anything like it been heard?
native_verses.4:33: Has any people heard the voice of God speaking from within the fire, just as you yourself heard, and lived?
native_verses.4:34: Or has a god ever attempted to come and take a nation for himself from the midst of another nation, with testings, with signs and wonders, with war, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
native_verses.4:35: You yourself were made to see, so that you would know that the LORD—He is God; there is no other apart from Him.
native_verses.4:36: From the heavens He caused you to hear His voice to discipline you, and on the earth He made you see His great fire, and you heard His words from within the fire.
native_verses.4:37: And because He loved your fathers and chose their seed after them, He brought you out by His presence, with His great strength, from Egypt,
native_verses.4:38: to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, to give to you their land as an inheritance, as on this day.
native_verses.4:39: So know today, and bring it back to your heart, that the LORD—He is God in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is no other.
native_verses.4:40: And keep His statutes and His commandments that I am commanding you today, so that it may be well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may prolong your days on the land that the LORD your God is giving to you for all time.
native_verses.4:41: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
native_verses.4:42: for a killer to flee there who kills his neighbor unintentionally and had not hated him previously, so that he might flee to one of these cities and live:
native_verses.4:43: Bezer in the wilderness, in the land of the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
native_verses.4:44: And this is the law that Moses placed before the sons of Israel.
native_verses.4:45: These are the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt,
native_verses.4:46: beyond the Jordan, in the valley facing Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who resided in Heshbon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel struck down when they came out of Egypt.
native_verses.4:47: And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan—the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise—
native_verses.4:48: from Aroer, which is on the rim of the Wadi Arnon, as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,
native_verses.4:49: and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastward, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, beneath the slopes of Pisgah.
native_verses.5:1: Moses called to all Israel and said to them, "Listen, Israel, to the statutes and the judgments that I am speaking in your ears today; learn them and take care to carry them out.
native_verses.5:2: The LORD our God cut a covenant with us at Horeb.
native_verses.5:3: It was not with our fathers that the LORD cut this covenant, but with us—we who are here today, all of us alive.
native_verses.5:4: Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from within the fire—
native_verses.5:5: I was standing between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up on the mountain—saying,
native_verses.5:6: 'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
native_verses.5:7: You must not have other gods in My presence.
native_verses.5:8: You must not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
native_verses.5:9: You must not bow down to them or serve them, because I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the guilt of fathers upon children, and upon the third and upon the fourth generations of those who hate Me,
native_verses.5:10: yet showing loyal love to thousands, to those who love Me and to those who keep My commandments.
native_verses.5:11: You must not take up the name of the LORD your God in vain, because the LORD will not acquit the one who takes up His name in vain.
native_verses.5:12: Keep the Sabbath day to consecrate it, just as the LORD your God commanded you.
native_verses.5:13: Six days you are to labor and carry out all your work,
native_verses.5:14: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God; you must not do any work—you, or your son, or your daughter, or your male slave, or your female slave, or your ox, or your donkey, or any of your livestock, or your foreign resident who is within your gates—so that your male slave and your female slave may rest just like you.
native_verses.5:15: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm. For this reason the LORD your God has commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
native_verses.5:16: Honor your father and your mother, just as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged and so that things may go well for you upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
native_verses.5:18: And you must not commit adultery.
native_verses.5:20: And you must not testify against your neighbor as a false witness.
native_verses.5:21: And you must not covet your neighbor's wife, and you must not crave your neighbor's house, his field, his male slave or his female slave, his ox or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.'
native_verses.5:22: These words the LORD spoke to your entire assembly on the mountain from within the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a loud voice, and He added nothing more. Then He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
native_verses.5:23: And when you heard the voice from within the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, you drew near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.
native_verses.5:24: And you said, 'Look, the LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and His voice we have heard from within the fire. This day we have seen that God speaks with man and he remains alive.
native_verses.5:25: And now, why should we die? For this great fire will devour us. If we continue hearing the voice of the LORD our God any further, we will die.
native_verses.5:26: For who among all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking from within the fire, as we have, and stayed alive?
native_verses.5:27: You draw near and listen to everything that the LORD our God says, and you speak to us everything that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will listen and do it.'
native_verses.5:28: Then the LORD heard the sound of your words as you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard the sound of the words of this people that they spoke to you; they have done well in all they have spoken.
native_verses.5:29: If only they had this heart in them to fear Me and to keep all My commandments always, so that things might go well for them and for their children forever!
native_verses.5:30: Go, tell them, "Go back to your tents."
native_verses.5:31: But as for you, stand here with Me, so that I may speak to you the entire commandment and the statutes and the judgments that you are to teach them, so that they may carry them out in the land that I am giving them to possess.'
native_verses.5:32: Therefore take care to do just as the LORD your God commanded you; you must not turn aside to the right or to the left.
native_verses.5:33: You must walk in the entire way that the LORD your God commanded you, so that you may live, and so that things may go well for you, and you may lengthen your days in the land that you will possess."
native_verses.6:1: Now this is the commandment, the statutes and the judgments, that the LORD your God commanded to be taught to you, to carry out in the land to which you are crossing over to possess it,
native_verses.6:2: so that you may fear the LORD your God—to keep all His statutes and His commandments that I am commanding you, you and your son and your son's son, all the days of your life—and so that your days may be prolonged.
native_verses.6:3: So listen, Israel, and take care to do so, that things may go well for you and that you may multiply greatly, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you—a land flowing with milk and honey.
native_verses.6:4: Listen, Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD is one.
native_verses.6:5: And you must love the LORD your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with all your might.
native_verses.6:6: And these words that I am commanding you today must be upon your heart.
native_verses.6:7: You must teach them repeatedly to your children and speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk along the way, and when you lie down, and when you get up.
native_verses.6:8: You must tie them as a sign upon your hand, and they are to be frontlets between your eyes.
native_verses.6:9: And you must write them upon the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
native_verses.6:10: And it will happen when the LORD your God brings you into the land that He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to you—great and good cities that you did not build,
native_verses.6:11: and houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, and hewn cisterns that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,
native_verses.6:12: then guard yourself so that you do not forget the LORD, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
native_verses.6:13: The LORD your God you must fear, and Him you must serve, and by His name you must swear.
native_verses.6:14: You must not go after other gods, from among the gods of the peoples who are all around you,
native_verses.6:15: for the LORD your God among you is a jealous God—or else the anger of the LORD your God will burn against you, and He will destroy you from the face of the earth.
native_verses.6:16: You must not test the LORD your God, just as you tested Him at Massah.
native_verses.6:17: You must carefully keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and His testimonies and His statutes that He commanded you.
native_verses.6:18: And you must do what is upright and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that things may go well for you, and so that you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD swore to your fathers,
native_verses.6:19: by thrusting out all your enemies from your presence, just as the LORD spoke.
native_verses.6:20: When your son asks you in the future, saying, "What are the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments that the LORD our God commanded you?"
native_verses.6:21: then you must say to your son, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand.
native_verses.6:22: And the LORD displayed signs and wonders, great and devastating, against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against his entire household, before our eyes.
native_verses.6:23: And He brought us out from there so that He might bring us in, to give us the land that He swore to our fathers.
native_verses.6:24: And the LORD commanded us to carry out all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God for our good always, to keep us alive just as on this day.
native_verses.6:25: And righteousness will be ours if we take care to carry out this entire commandment before the LORD our God, just as He commanded us."
native_verses.7:1: When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to take possession of, and He dislodges many nations from before you—the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—seven nations more numerous and more powerful than you,
native_verses.7:2: and when the LORD your God gives them over before you and you strike them down, you must wholly devote them to destruction. You must not make a covenant with them, and you must not show them favor.
native_verses.7:3: You must not intermarry with them: you must not give your daughter to his son, nor take his daughter for your son.
native_verses.7:4: For he will turn your son away from following Me, and they will serve other gods; then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will swiftly wipe you out.
native_verses.7:5: Instead, this is what you must do to them: you must pull down their altars, shatter their standing stones, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images in the fire.
native_verses.7:6: For you are a holy people for the LORD your God; it is you whom the LORD your God has chosen to be a treasured people for Himself from among all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
native_verses.7:7: It was not because you were more numerous than all the peoples that the LORD set His affection on you and chose you, since you were the fewest among all the peoples.
native_verses.7:8: Rather, because of the LORD's love for you and because He kept the oath He swore to your fathers, the LORD brought you out by a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slaves, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
native_verses.7:9: So you must know that the LORD your God—He is God, the faithful God who keeps the covenant and loyal love for those who love Him and for those who keep His commandments, to a thousand generations,
native_verses.7:10: and who repays those who hate Him to their face in order to destroy them; He will not delay with one who hates Him—to his face He will repay him.
native_verses.7:11: So you must keep the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that I command you today, by doing them.
native_verses.7:12: Then it will happen that because you listen to these judgments, and keep them and do them, the LORD your God will keep for you the covenant and the loyal love that He swore to your fathers.
native_verses.7:13: He will love you, bless you, and make you numerous; He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your soil—your grain, your new wine, and your fresh oil, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock—on the land that He swore to your fathers to give you.
native_verses.7:14: You will be blessed more than all the peoples; there will be neither barren male nor barren female among you, nor among your livestock.
native_verses.7:15: The LORD will remove every illness from you, and He will not place on you any of the dreadful diseases of Egypt that you knew, but will put them on all those who hate you.
native_verses.7:16: You must devour all the peoples whom the LORD your God is giving to you; your eye must show no pity on them, and you must not serve their gods, for that will be a snare to you.
native_verses.7:17: If you say in your heart, "These nations are more numerous than I am; how will I be able to dispossess them?"
native_verses.7:18: you must not be afraid of them; be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:
native_verses.7:19: the great tests that your eyes saw, the signs and the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm, with which the LORD your God brought you out; in the same way the LORD your God will do to all the peoples before whom you are afraid.
native_verses.7:20: Furthermore, the LORD your God will send the hornet among them until those who remain and those who hide themselves from before you perish.
native_verses.7:21: You must not be terrified before them, because the LORD your God is among you—a great and fearsome God.
native_verses.7:22: The LORD your God will dislodge these nations from before you little by little; you will not be able to finish them off swiftly, or else the wild animals of the field will multiply against you.
native_verses.7:23: But the LORD your God will give them over before you and throw them into a massive panic until they are wiped out.
native_verses.7:24: He will put their kings into your hand, and you will cause their name to perish from beneath the heavens; no man will stand firm before you until you have wiped them out.
native_verses.7:25: You must burn the carved images of their gods in the fire. Do not covet the silver and gold on them and take it for yourself, so that you are not ensnared by it; for it is a detestable thing to the LORD your God.
native_verses.7:26: You must not bring a detestable thing into your house, or you will become a thing devoted to destruction just like it; you must completely loathe it and completely detest it, for it is a thing devoted to destruction.
native_verses.8:1: The entire commandment that I am commanding you today you must take care to do, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your fathers.
native_verses.8:2: And you must remember the entire way along which the LORD your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart—whether you would keep His commandments or not.
native_verses.8:3: So He humbled you, caused you to go hungry, and fed you the manna that you did not know and your fathers did not know, in order to make you know that not on bread alone does a human being live, but on everything that goes forth from the mouth of the LORD does a human being live.
native_verses.8:4: Your garment did not wear away on you, and your foot did not become swollen these forty years.
native_verses.8:5: You must know within your heart, then, that just as a man disciplines his son, the LORD your God is disciplining you.
native_verses.8:6: So keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and fearing Him.
native_verses.8:7: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of springs and deep waters flowing out in the valley and in the hill country;
native_verses.8:8: a land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of oil-bearing olives and honey;
native_verses.8:9: a land where you will not eat bread in scarcity and will not lack anything in it; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose mountains you will mine copper.
native_verses.8:10: Once you have eaten and are satisfied, you must bless the LORD your God on account of the good land that He gave you.
native_verses.8:11: Watch yourself so that you do not forget the LORD your God by failing to keep His commandments, His judgments, and His statutes that I command you today;
native_verses.8:12: or else, after you have eaten and are satisfied, and build good houses and inhabit them,
native_verses.8:13: and your cattle and your flock multiply, and silver and gold multiply for you, and everything that belongs to you multiplies,
native_verses.8:14: then your heart will become lifted up, and you will forget the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves,
native_verses.8:15: who led you through the great and fearsome wilderness of fiery serpents, scorpions, and parched ground where there was no water; who brought water out for you from the flint rock,
native_verses.8:16: who fed you manna in the wilderness that your fathers did not know, in order to humble you and in order to test you, so as to do good to you in your future;
native_verses.8:17: and you will say in your heart, "My strength and the might of my hand have produced this wealth for me."
native_verses.8:18: Rather, you must remember the LORD your God, for it is He who gives you strength to produce wealth, in order to uphold His covenant that He swore to your fathers, as it is today.
native_verses.8:19: And it will come about that if you indeed forget the LORD your God, and walk after other gods, and serve them and bow down to them, I bear witness against you today that you will certainly perish.
native_verses.8:20: Just like the nations whom the LORD is causing to perish from before you, in the same way you will perish, because you will not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
native_verses.9:1: Listen, Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan to go in and take possession of nations greater and mightier than you, large cities fortified up to the heavens,
native_verses.9:2: a great and tall people, the sons of the Anakim, whom you know and about whom you have heard, "Who can stand firm before the sons of Anak?"
native_verses.9:3: So know today that the LORD your God is the One crossing over ahead of you as a devouring fire; He will wipe them out, and He will subdue them before you. Then you will dispossess them and cause them to perish quickly, just as the LORD spoke to you.
native_verses.9:4: Do not say in your heart, when the LORD your God thrusts them out from before you, "Because of my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to take possession of this land." Rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is dispossessing them from before you.
native_verses.9:5: It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to take possession of their land; instead, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD your God is dispossessing them from before you, and in order to uphold the word that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
native_verses.9:6: So know that it is not on account of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving this good land to you to take possession of it, because you are a stiff-necked people.
native_verses.9:7: Remember, do not forget how you provoked the LORD your God to wrath in the wilderness; from the day you went out from the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.
native_verses.9:8: At Horeb as well, you provoked the LORD to wrath, and the LORD grew angry enough with you to wipe you out.
native_verses.9:9: When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD had made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water.
native_verses.9:10: Then the LORD gave to me the two stone tablets, written with the finger of God; on them were all the very words that the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from within the fire on the day of the assembly.
native_verses.9:11: At the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave to me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.
native_verses.9:12: And the LORD said to me, "Get up, go down quickly from here, because your people whom you brought out of Egypt have corrupted themselves. They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a cast image."
native_verses.9:13: Then the LORD said to me, "I have seen this people, and look, they are a stiff-necked people.
native_verses.9:14: Leave Me alone, so that I may wipe them out and erase their name from beneath the heavens; and I will make you into a nation mightier and more numerous than they."
native_verses.9:15: Then I turned and went down from the mountain, as the mountain was blazing with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my two hands.
native_verses.9:16: I saw, and look, you had sinned against the LORD your God: you had made for yourselves a cast calf; you had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
native_verses.9:17: So I grasped the two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and shattered them before your eyes.
native_verses.9:18: Then I fell prostrate before the LORD as at the first, forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water, on account of all your sin that you had sinned, in doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD to provoke Him to anger.
native_verses.9:19: For I dreaded the anger and fury with which the LORD was wrathful against you, so as to wipe you out. Yet the LORD listened to me that time as well.
native_verses.9:20: And the LORD grew very angry with Aaron, so as to wipe him out; so I prayed on behalf of Aaron as well at that time.
native_verses.9:21: Then I took your sin that you had made, the calf, and burned it in the fire; I pounded it, grinding it thoroughly until it became fine dust, and I threw its dust into the stream coming down from the mountain.
native_verses.9:22: And at Taberah, and at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, you kept provoking the LORD to wrath.
