native_verses.28:30: You will betroth a woman, yet another man will lie with her; you will build a house, yet you will not live in it; you will plant a vineyard, yet you will not enjoy its produce.
native_verses.28:31: Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, yet you will not eat from it; your donkey will be seized from before you and will not return to you; your flock will be given to your enemies, and you will have no rescuer.
native_verses.28:32: Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes watch and pine away for them all day long, and there will be no power in your hand.
native_verses.28:33: A people whom you have not known will eat the fruit of your soil and all your toil, and you will be only oppressed and crushed all the time.
native_verses.28:34: And you will go mad from the sight of your eyes that you will see.
native_verses.28:35: The LORD will strike you with malignant boils on the knees and on the legs, from which you will not be able to be healed, from the sole of your foot even to the top of your head.
native_verses.28:36: The LORD will lead you and your king whom you appoint over yourself to a nation that you and your fathers have not known, and there you will serve other gods—wood and stone.
native_verses.28:37: And you will become an object of shock, a proverb, and a taunt among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
native_verses.28:38: You will take out much seed to the field, yet you will gather little, because the locust will devour it.
native_verses.28:39: You will plant vineyards and tend them, yet you will not drink wine nor gather the harvest, because the worm will eat it.
native_verses.28:40: You will have olive trees in all your territory, yet you will not rub yourself with oil, because your olives will fall off.
native_verses.28:41: You will father sons and daughters, yet they will not belong to you, because they will go into captivity.
native_verses.28:42: The cricket will take possession of all your trees and the fruit of your soil.
native_verses.28:43: The resident alien who is in your midst will ascend above you higher and higher, while you will descend lower and lower.
native_verses.28:44: He will lend to you, yet you will not lend to him; he will become the head, and you will become the tail.
native_verses.28:45: And all these curses will come on you and pursue you and catch up with you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep His commands and His statutes that He commanded you.
native_verses.28:46: And they will be upon you as a sign and a wonder, and upon your seed forever.
native_verses.28:47: Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart for the abundance of everything,
native_verses.28:48: you will serve your enemies whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in the lack of everything; and He will place an iron yoke upon your neck until He destroys you.
native_verses.28:49: The LORD will raise up a nation against you from far away, from the end of the earth, just as the eagle swoops, a nation whose language you will not understand,
native_verses.28:50: a fierce-faced nation that will show no regard for the elderly and will show no pity to the young.
native_verses.28:51: And it will eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your soil until you are destroyed; it will not leave you grain, new wine, or fresh oil, nor the offspring of your cattle or the increase of your flock, until it causes you to perish.
native_verses.28:52: And it will besiege you in all your gates until your high and fortified walls in which you trust come down across all your land; and it will besiege you in all your gates across all your land that the LORD your God has given you.
native_verses.28:53: Then you will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press hard on you.
native_verses.28:54: The man among you who is tender and very delicate—his eye will turn begrudging toward his brother, toward the wife of his bosom, and toward the rest of his children whom he leaves remaining,
native_verses.28:55: so that he will not give to any of them from the flesh of his children that he is eating, because nothing has been left to him, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press hard on you in all your gates.
native_verses.28:56: The woman among you who is tender and delicate, who would not attempt to place the sole of her foot on the ground out of delicacy and tenderness—her eye will turn begrudging toward the husband of her bosom, toward her son, and toward her daughter,
native_verses.28:57: and toward her afterbirth that comes out from between her feet and toward her children whom she bears, because she will eat them in secret in the lack of everything, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press hard on you in your gates.
native_verses.28:58: If you do not take care to carry out all the words of this law written in this book, to fear this glorious and fearsome name, the LORD your God,
native_verses.28:59: then the LORD will make your afflictions and the afflictions of your seed extraordinary—great and enduring afflictions, and severe and enduring sicknesses.
native_verses.28:60: And He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.
native_verses.28:61: Even every sickness and every affliction that is not written in the book of this law, the LORD will bring them on you until you are destroyed.
native_verses.28:62: And you will be left few in number, whereas you had been like the stars of the heavens in multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
native_verses.28:63: And it will come about that just as the LORD rejoiced over you to do good to you and to multiply you, so the LORD will rejoice over you to cause you to perish and to destroy you; and you will be uprooted from the land that you are entering to possess.
native_verses.28:64: And the LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth, and there you will serve other gods that you and your fathers have not known—wood and stone.
native_verses.28:65: And among those nations you will find no repose, and there will be no place of rest for the sole of your foot; and there the LORD will give you a quaking heart, pining of eyes, and despair of soul.
native_verses.28:66: And your life will hang in suspense before you; you will feel dread night and day, and you will have no certainty of your life.
native_verses.28:67: In the morning you will say, "I wish it were evening!" and in the evening you will say, "I wish it were morning!" because of the dread of your heart that you will feel and the sight of your eyes that you will see.
native_verses.28:68: And the LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way of which I told you, "You will not see it again." And there you will put yourselves up for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, with no buyer.
native_verses.28:69: These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant that He made with them at Horeb.
native_verses.29:1: Then Moses called to all Israel and said to them, "You yourselves saw everything that the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,
native_verses.29:2: the great testings that your eyes saw, those great signs and wonders.
native_verses.29:3: Yet the LORD has not given you a heart to know, or eyes to see, or ears to hear, until this day.
native_verses.29:4: And I led you for forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not wear out on you, and your sandal did not wear out on your foot.
native_verses.29:5: You did not eat bread, nor did you drink wine or intoxicating drink, so that you would know that I am the LORD your God.
native_verses.29:6: Then you came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us for battle, and we struck them down.
native_verses.29:7: And we took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, to the Gadites, and to half the tribe of the Manassites.
native_verses.29:8: Therefore you shall keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may succeed in everything that you do.
native_verses.29:9: You are standing today, all of you, before the LORD your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, every man of Israel,
native_verses.29:10: your little ones, your wives, and your resident alien who is in the midst of your camps, from the cutter of your wood to the drawer of your water,
native_verses.29:11: so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God and into His oath, which the LORD your God is making with you today,
native_verses.29:12: in order to establish you today for Himself as a people, and that He may be God to you, just as He spoke to you and just as He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
native_verses.29:13: And it is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath,
native_verses.29:14: but with the one who is here with us standing today before the LORD our God, and with the one who is not here with us today—
native_verses.29:15: for you yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed,
native_verses.29:16: and you saw their detestable things and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were with them—
native_verses.29:17: so that there may not be among you a man or woman, or a clan or tribe, whose heart is turning away today from the LORD our God to go to serve the gods of those nations, so that there may not be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood.
native_verses.29:18: And it will be, when he hears the words of this sworn curse, that he will bless himself in his heart, saying, 'Peace will be mine, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart'—so as to sweep away the watered with the dry.
native_verses.29:19: The LORD will not be willing to pardon him; rather, then the anger of the LORD and His jealousy will smoke against that man, and every sworn curse written in this book will lie upon him, and the LORD will wipe out his name from under the heavens.
native_verses.29:20: And the LORD will set him apart for calamity from all the tribes of Israel, according to all the sworn curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.
native_verses.29:21: And the coming generation, your children who will rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land will say, when they see the plagues of that land and its sicknesses with which the LORD has made it sick—
native_verses.29:22: all its land is sulfur and salt, a burned waste; it is not sown, nor does it bring forth growth, nor does any plant come up in it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in His anger and in His wrath—
native_verses.29:23: all the nations will say, 'Why has the LORD done so to this land? What is this great burning of anger?'
native_verses.29:24: And they will say, 'Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out from the land of Egypt,
native_verses.29:25: and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods that they did not know and that He had not apportioned to them.
native_verses.29:26: So the anger of the LORD burned against that land, to bring upon it the entire curse written in this book;
native_verses.29:27: and the LORD uprooted them from their soil in anger, and in wrath, and in great fury, and hurled them into another land, as it is this day.'
native_verses.29:28: The hidden things belong to the LORD our God, while the revealed things belong to us and to our children forever, to do all the words of this law."
native_verses.30:1: "And it will be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I have placed before you, and you call them back to your heart among all the nations to which the LORD your God has banished you,
native_verses.30:2: and you return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice according to everything that I am commanding you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,
native_verses.30:3: then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and show compassion to you, and He will again gather you from all the peoples to which the LORD your God has scattered you.
native_verses.30:4: If your banished ones are at the end of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there He will take you.
native_verses.30:5: And the LORD your God will bring you to the land that your fathers possessed, and you will possess it; and He will make you prosper and make you more numerous than your fathers.
native_verses.30:6: Then the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, for the sake of your life.
native_verses.30:7: And the LORD your God will place all these sworn curses upon your enemies and upon those who hate you, who pursued you.
native_verses.30:8: And you yourself will again listen to the voice of the LORD, and do all His commandments that I am commanding you today.
native_verses.30:9: Then the LORD your God will make you abound in every work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your soil, for good; for the LORD will again delight over you for good, just as He delighted over your fathers,
native_verses.30:10: if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep His commandments and His statutes that are written in this book of the law, if you return to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
native_verses.30:11: For this commandment that I am commanding you today is not beyond you, nor is it far away.
native_verses.30:12: It is not in the heavens, for anyone to say, 'Who will go up for us to the heavens and get it for us, and cause us to hear it, so that we may do it?'
native_verses.30:13: Nor is it beyond the sea, for anyone to say, 'Who will cross over for us to the other side of the sea and get it for us, and cause us to hear it, so that we may do it?'
native_verses.30:14: Rather, the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, for you to do it.
native_verses.30:15: Look, I have placed before you today life and good, and death and evil,
native_verses.30:16: in that I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments and His statutes and His ordinances; then you will live and become numerous, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land that you are entering to possess.
native_verses.30:17: But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away and bow down to other gods and serve them,
native_verses.30:18: I announce to you today that you will certainly perish; you will not prolong your days on the land that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
native_verses.30:19: I summon the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you today: life and death I have placed before you, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, therefore, so that you may live, you and your seed,
native_verses.30:20: loving the LORD your God, listening to His voice, and clinging to Him; for He is your life and the length of your days, so that you may live on the land that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to them."
native_verses.31:1: And Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
native_verses.31:2: He said to them, "I am one hundred and twenty years old today; I can no longer go out and come in, and the LORD has said to me, 'You shall not cross over this Jordan.'
native_verses.31:3: The LORD your God Himself is crossing over before you; He will destroy these nations from before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua himself is crossing over before you, just as the LORD has spoken.
native_verses.31:4: And the LORD will do to them just as He did to Sihon and to Og, kings of the Amorites, and to their land, whom He destroyed.
native_verses.31:5: And the LORD will give them over before you, and you are to do to them according to the entire commandment that I have commanded you.
native_verses.31:6: Be strong and take courage; do not fear and do not tremble before them, for the LORD your God Himself is the One going with you; He will not let go of you, and He will not abandon you."
native_verses.31:7: Then Moses called to Joshua and said to him before the eyes of all Israel, "Be strong and take courage, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their fathers to give to them, and you will cause them to inherit it.
native_verses.31:8: And the LORD Himself is the One going before you; He will be with you. He will not let go of you, and He will not abandon you. Do not fear, and do not be dismayed."
native_verses.31:9: And Moses wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, the bearers of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
native_verses.31:10: Then Moses commanded them, saying, "At the end of every seven years, at the appointed time of the year of release, during the Feast of Booths,
native_verses.31:11: when all Israel comes to appear in the presence of the LORD your God in the place that He will choose, you are to read this law before all Israel in their hearing.
native_verses.31:12: Assemble the people—the men, the women, the little ones, and your resident alien who is within your gates—so that they may hear and so that they may learn, and fear the LORD your God, and take care to do all the words of this law.
native_verses.31:13: And their children, who have not known, will hear and learn to fear the LORD your God all the days that you live on the land that you are crossing over the Jordan to possess."
native_verses.31:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Look, the days have drawn near for you to die. Call Joshua, and station yourselves in the tent of meeting, so that I may commission him." So Moses and Joshua went and stationed themselves in the tent of meeting.
native_verses.31:15: Then the LORD appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the doorway of the tent.
native_verses.31:16: And the LORD said to Moses, "Look, you are about to lie down with your fathers; and this people will rise up and prostitute themselves after the foreign gods of the land into whose midst they are going, and they will abandon Me and break My covenant that I made with them.
native_verses.31:17: Then My anger will burn against them on that day, and I will abandon them and hide My face from them, and they will be devoured. And many calamities and distresses will overtake them, and they will say on that day, 'Is it not because our God is not in our midst that these calamities have overtaken us?'
native_verses.31:18: And I will certainly hide My face on that day on account of all the evil that they have done, for they have turned to other gods.
native_verses.31:19: And now, write down this song for yourselves, and teach it to the sons of Israel; place it in their mouths, in order that this song may be a witness for Me against the sons of Israel.
native_verses.31:20: For when I bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to their fathers, and they eat and are filled and grow fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them, and they will treat Me with contempt and break My covenant.
native_verses.31:21: And it will come about, when many calamities and distresses overtake them, that this song will testify before them as a witness—for it will not be forgotten from the mouth of their seed—for I know their inclination, which they are forming today, before I bring them into the land of which I swore."
native_verses.31:22: Then Moses wrote down this song on that day and taught it to the sons of Israel.
native_verses.31:23: And He commissioned Joshua the son of Nun and said, "Be strong and take courage, for you will bring the sons of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I Myself will be with you."
native_verses.31:24: And it happened, when Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book to their completion,
native_verses.31:25: that Moses commanded the Levites, the bearers of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, saying,
native_verses.31:26: "Take this book of the law and place it at the side of the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and it will be there as a witness against you.
native_verses.31:27: For I myself know your rebellion and your stiff neck; look, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD—how much more after my death!
native_verses.31:28: Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, so that I may speak these words in their hearing and summon the heavens and the earth to witness against them.
native_verses.31:29: For I know that after my death you will certainly act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I have commanded you, and calamity will come upon you in the latter days, because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, so as to provoke Him to anger by the work of your hands."
native_verses.31:30: Then Moses spoke in the hearing of the entire assembly of Israel the words of this song to their completion.
native_verses.32:1: Listen attentively, heavens, and I will speak, and let the earth hear the utterances of my mouth.
native_verses.32:2: May my instruction drip like rain, may my speech flow like dew, like light rain upon fresh grass, and like abundant showers upon green plants.
native_verses.32:3: For I will call out the name of the LORD; give greatness to our God!
native_verses.32:4: The Rock—flawless is His work, for all His ways are justice; a God of faithfulness, and there is no wrongdoing; He is righteous and upright.
native_verses.32:5: They have behaved corruptly toward Him; they are not His children—the blemish is theirs, a crooked and warped generation.
native_verses.32:6: Is it to the LORD that you repay this, foolish people without wisdom? Is He not your Father who acquired you? He made you and established you.
native_verses.32:7: Remember the ancient days; discern the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will report it to you; your elders, and they will speak to you.
native_verses.32:8: When the Most High gave inheritances to the nations, when He separated the sons of Adam, He fixed the borders of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
native_verses.32:9: For the share of the LORD is His people; Jacob is the measured lot of His inheritance.
native_verses.32:10: He found him in a wilderness land, and in a desolate, howling wasteland; He surrounded him, He attended to him, He protected him like the pupil of His eye.
native_verses.32:11: Like an eagle that rouses its nest and hovers over its fledglings, He spread out His wings, took him, and bore him upon His pinions.
native_verses.32:12: The LORD by Himself led him, and with Him there was no foreign god.
native_verses.32:13: He caused him to ride upon the heights of the earth, and he ate the yield of the field; He nursed him with honey from the crag, and oil from the flint rock,
native_verses.32:14: curds of cattle and milk of the flock, along with the fat of lambs, rams that are offspring of Bashan, and male goats, along with the fat of the kidneys of wheat; and you drank the blood of the grape, foaming wine.
native_verses.32:15: Then Jeshurun grew fat and kicked—you grew fat, you grew thick, you were gorged—and he abandoned God who made him, and treated with contempt the Rock of his salvation.
native_verses.32:16: They roused Him to jealousy with alien gods; with abominations they angered Him.
native_verses.32:17: They sacrificed to demons, which are not God—to gods they did not know, new ones that arrived recently, before whom your fathers did not shudder.
native_verses.32:18: The Rock who fathered you, you neglected, and you forgot the God who brought you forth.
native_verses.32:19: The LORD saw it and scorned them, because of the vexation of His sons and His daughters.
native_verses.32:20: And He said, "I will conceal My face from them; I will see what their outcome will be, for they are a generation of perversity, children with no faithfulness in them.
native_verses.32:21: They have roused Me to jealousy with what is not a god; they have angered Me with their worthless things. So I Myself will rouse them to jealousy with those who are not a people; with a foolish nation I will anger them.
native_verses.32:22: For a fire has flared up in My anger, and it blazes all the way to the lowest Sheol; it devours the earth and its produce, and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
native_verses.32:23: I will pile calamities upon them; My arrows I will exhaust against them.
native_verses.32:24: They will be drained by famine, devoured by burning fever and bitter pestilence; the teeth of beasts I will let loose against them, along with the venom of creatures crawling in the dust.
native_verses.32:25: From outside, the sword will bereave, and from within the chambers, terror—both young man and virgin, the nursing infant along with the gray-haired man.
native_verses.32:26: I said, 'I would cleave them in pieces; I would cause their remembrance to cease from humanity,'
native_verses.32:27: had I not dreaded the vexation of the enemy, that their foes might misinterpret it, that they might say, 'Our hand has risen high, and it was not the LORD who performed all this.'"
native_verses.32:28: For they are a nation bereft of counsel, and in them there is no discernment.
native_verses.32:29: If only they were wise, they would comprehend this; they would discern their outcome!
native_verses.32:30: How could one pursue a thousand, and two drive ten thousand into flight, unless their Rock had sold them, and the LORD had handed them over?
native_verses.32:31: For their rock is not like our Rock, and our enemies themselves are judges.
native_verses.32:32: For from the vine of Sodom is their vine, and from the terraced fields of Gomorrah; their grapes are grapes of poison, and clusters of bitterness are theirs.
native_verses.32:33: The venom of serpents is their wine, and the cruel poison of cobras.
native_verses.32:34: "Is it not stored away with Me, sealed in My storehouses?
native_verses.32:35: Mine are vengeance and repayment, for the time when their foot totters; for the day of their ruin is near, and the things prepared for them are hastening on."
native_verses.32:36: For the LORD will render justice for His people, and He will feel compassion for His servants, when He sees that strength has vanished and no one remains, neither restrained nor free.
native_verses.32:37: Then He will say, "Where are their gods—the rock where they sought refuge,
native_verses.32:38: who used to eat the fat of their sacrifices and drink the wine of their drink offering? Let them arise and aid you; let them be a shelter over you!
native_verses.32:39: See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me; I Myself put to death and bring to life; I have wounded, and I Myself will heal, and there is no one who rescues from My hand.
native_verses.32:40: For I raise My hand to heaven and say, 'As I live forever,
native_verses.32:41: when I sharpen the flash of My sword and My hand grasps justice, I will return vengeance to My foes, and those who hate Me I will repay.
native_verses.32:42: I will make My arrows drunk on blood, and My sword will devour flesh—from the blood of the killed and the captives, from the unshorn heads of the enemy.'"
native_verses.32:43: Acclaim His people, nations, for He will avenge the blood of His servants; He will return vengeance to His foes, and will make atonement for His land, His people.
native_verses.32:44: Then Moses came and spoke all the words of this song within the hearing of the people, he and Hoshea the son of Nun.
native_verses.32:45: And Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel.
native_verses.32:46: Then he said to them, "Set your heart on all the words that I am testifying to you today, so that you may command them to your children, to observe and carry out all the words of this law.
native_verses.32:47: For it is not an empty word for you; rather, it is your life, and through this word you will lengthen your days upon the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
native_verses.32:48: Then the LORD spoke to Moses on that very day, saying,
native_verses.32:49: "Ascend to this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab facing Jericho, and view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the sons of Israel as a possession.
native_verses.32:50: And die upon the mountain you are ascending, and be gathered to your kin, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his kin,
native_verses.32:51: because you acted unfaithfully against Me among the sons of Israel at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin—because you did not regard Me as holy among the sons of Israel.
native_verses.32:52: For from a distance you will see the land, yet you will not enter there—into the land that I am giving to the sons of Israel."
native_verses.33:1: And this is the blessing by which Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel before his death.
native_verses.33:2: And he said, "The LORD came from Sinai and rose from Seir upon them; He blazed forth from Mount Paran and arrived from myriads of holy ones; from His right hand was a fiery law for them.
native_verses.33:3: Truly, He loves the peoples; all His holy ones are in Your hand; they settled down at Your feet, and each one receives from Your words.
native_verses.33:4: Moses commanded a law for us, a possession for the congregation of Jacob.
native_verses.33:5: And He became king in Jeshurun as the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel as one.
native_verses.33:6: May Reuben live and not die, and may his men not be few."
native_verses.33:7: And this is for Judah; he said, "Hear Judah's voice, LORD, and bring him to his people. With his own hands he strives for himself, and may You be a help against his foes."
native_verses.33:8: And concerning Levi he said, "Your Thummim and Your Urim belong to Your faithful man, whom You tested at Massah, with whom You strove at the waters of Meribah;
native_verses.33:9: who said regarding his father and his mother, 'I have not seen him,' and did not recognize his brothers, and did not know his sons; for they kept Your word and guard Your covenant.
native_verses.33:10: They shall teach Your judgments to Jacob and Your law to Israel; they shall set incense before Your nostrils and a whole burnt offering on Your altar.
native_verses.33:11: Bless his strength, LORD, and be pleased with the work of his hands; crush the loins of those who rise against him and of those who hate him, so that they may not rise."
native_verses.33:12: Concerning Benjamin he said, "The beloved of the LORD shall dwell in safety beside Him; He shields him all day long, and between his shoulders He dwells."
native_verses.33:13: And concerning Joseph he said, "Blessed by the LORD is his land, with the choice bounty of the heavens, with dew, and with the deep that lies beneath,
native_verses.33:14: and with the choice bounty of the yields of the sun, and with the choice bounty thrust forth by the months,
native_verses.33:15: and with the finest of the ancient mountains, and with the choice bounty of the everlasting hills,
native_verses.33:16: and with the choice bounty of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of the One who dwelt in the bush. May it come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the head of the one set apart among his brothers.
native_verses.33:17: The firstborn of his bull—splendor belongs to him, and the horns of a wild ox are his horns; with them he will gore peoples together, to the ends of the earth. And these are the myriads of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh."
native_verses.33:18: And concerning Zebulun he said, "Rejoice, Zebulun, when you go out, and Issachar, in your tents.
native_verses.33:19: They will summon peoples to the mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they will draw in the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures buried in the sand."
native_verses.33:20: And concerning Gad he said, "Blessed is the One who enlarges Gad; he dwells like a lion and tears the arm, indeed the crown of the head.
native_verses.33:21: And he selected the first portion for himself, for there a commander's allotment was reserved; and he arrived with the heads of the people; he carried out the righteousness of the LORD, and His judgments with Israel."
native_verses.33:22: And concerning Dan he said, "Dan is a lion cub; he springs forth from Bashan."
native_verses.33:23: And concerning Naphtali he said, "Naphtali, satisfied with favor and filled with the LORD's blessing, possess the sea and the south."
native_verses.33:24: And concerning Asher he said, "Blessed above sons is Asher; let him be the favored one of his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.
native_verses.33:25: Iron and bronze shall be your bolts, and according to your days shall your strength be.
native_verses.33:26: There is no one like God, Jeshurun, who rides the heavens for your help, and in His majesty, the skies.
native_verses.33:27: A dwelling place is the ancient God, and beneath are everlasting arms; He expelled the enemy from before you and said, 'Destroy!'
native_verses.33:28: Thus Israel dwells in safety—the spring of Jacob alone—in a land of grain and new wine; indeed, his heavens drip dew.
native_verses.33:29: Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help and the One who is the sword of your majesty! Your enemies will cringe before you, and upon their high places you will tread."
native_verses.34:1: And Moses ascended from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah that faces Jericho. And the LORD showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
native_verses.34:2: and all of Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and the whole land of Judah as far as the western sea,
native_verses.34:3: and the Negev, and the Plain—the valley of Jericho, the city of palms—as far as Zoar.
native_verses.34:4: And the LORD said to him, "This is the land about which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give it.' I have caused you to see it with your own eyes, yet you shall not cross over there."
native_verses.34:5: And there Moses, the servant of the LORD, died in the land of Moab, at the LORD's command.
native_verses.34:6: And He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, across from Beth-peor; yet no one knows his burial site to this day.
native_verses.34:7: And Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye had not grown dim, and his vitality had not fled.
native_verses.34:8: And the sons of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days; then the days of weeping in mourning for Moses were completed.
native_verses.34:9: And Joshua, the son of Nun, was full of a spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands upon him; so the sons of Israel heeded him and did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
native_verses.34:10: And no prophet like Moses has arisen again in Israel, whom the LORD knew face to face,
native_verses.34:11: in all the signs and the wonders that the LORD sent him to perform in the land of Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against all his servants, and against his whole land,
native_verses.34:12: and in all the mighty hand and in all the great awe-inspiring work that Moses performed before the eyes of all Israel.

native_notes.1:4: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "in Ashtaroth, at Edrei" without a conjunction before "at Edrei," indicating where Og resided and where he was defeated, whereas the Septuagint inserts "and."
native_notes.1:17: "Show favoritism" renders the Hebrew idiom "recognize faces" (Hiphil of nakar with panim), denoting partiality in legal judgment.
native_notes.1:35: Following the oath verb in 1:34, the Hebrew particle im ("if") introduces a standard negative oath formula with an omitted self-imprecation, giving the emphatic sense "Not a man... shall see."
native_notes.1:41: "Considered it a light thing" translates a unique Hiphil form of the root hun (occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible), meaning to regard a task as easy or treat it lightly.
native_notes.1:46: "For as many days as you stayed" preserves the Hebrew idem per idem idiom (literally "like the days that you stayed"), used to summarize an extended period already known to the listeners.
native_notes.2:6: The Hebrew uses two distinct Qal verbs here: shavar ("buy grain/food," cf. its Hiphil "sell food" in 2:28) and the rare verb karah ("purchase/trade for," distinct from the homonymous karah "dig").
native_notes.2:13: Hebrew nachal ("wadi") denotes a seasonal stream-bed and its valley or gorge, distinguishing it from gay ("valley") in 3:29.
native_notes.2:15: "Rout them" translates le-hummam, the Qal infinitive construct of hamam ("throw into panic, rout, crush"), portraying divine judgment driving the rebellious generation out of the camp until they perished.
native_notes.2:33: The Masoretic text spells "his sons" defectively as banaw (without the yod of the plural suffix -ayw), though its vocalization reads the plural "his sons" rather than singular "his son."
native_notes.2:34: "Devoted to complete destruction" translates the Hiphil of charam (the cherem ban), denoting the irreversible setting apart of a conquered population or city to the LORD for total destruction.
native_notes.3:8: Hebrew be-ever ha-Yarden ("beyond the Jordan") literally means "across/on the side of the Jordan" and shifts perspective within this chapter—referring to the eastern side here, and to the western side (Canaan) in 3:20 and 3:25.
native_notes.3:14: Havvoth-jair (Hebrew Chavvot Ya'ir) literally means "tent-villages of Jair."
native_notes.3:16: Hebrew tokh ha-nachal u-gevul (literally "the middle of the wadi and a border") uses an explicative waw idiomatically to define the boundary line itself, as also in "with the Jordan as a border" in 3:17.
native_notes.3:26: "Was furious with me" translates va-yit'abber, the Hithpael of avar II ("be furious, overflow with wrath"), forming a sharp wordplay with the homonymous Qal verb avar I ("cross over") in Moses's plea in 3:25 and God's refusal in 3:27.
native_notes.4:7: The Hebrew phrase for "a god so close" pairs a grammatically plural adjective with the morphologically plural noun for deity, and can be rendered either "a god so close" or "gods so close."
native_notes.4:13: Literally "the ten words," the Hebrew phrase traditionally referred to as the Ten Commandments.
native_notes.4:23: The Piel verb rendered "has forbidden you" literally means "commanded you," used elliptically in a prohibition for "commanded you not to make."
native_notes.4:37: The Masoretic Hebrew literally has singular suffixes, "his seed after him," functioning as a collective or distributive singular after plural "your fathers."
native_notes.4:48: Mount Sion reflects the Masoretic spelling Si'on, which is distinct from Jerusalem's Zion and is likely a variant of Sirion in Deuteronomy 3:9, another name for Mount Hermon.
native_notes.5:5: This verse forms a parenthetical aside in Hebrew interrupting 'spoke' in 5:4 and 'saying' at the end of 5:5, which introduces the LORD's words in 5:6-21.
native_notes.5:10: Qere reads 'My commandments,' matching first-person 'those who love Me'; ketiv writes 'His commandments' (or 'His commandment').
native_notes.5:17: Native Masoretic order places "You must not murder" at 5:17 before "And you must not commit adultery" at 5:18; in the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 5:17 maps to slot 5:18 and MT 5:18 maps to slot 5:17.
native_notes.5:18: Native Masoretic order places "You must not murder" at 5:17 (without initial waw) and "And you must not commit adultery" at 5:18 (beginning the syndetic waw chain of vv. 18–21). In the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 5:18 maps to slot 5:17 and MT 5:17 maps to slot 5:18.
native_notes.5:27: The second Hebrew pronoun 'you' (ve'att) is spelled and pointed in the shortened form normally used for the feminine singular, a rare Masoretic masculine usage also found in Numbers 11:15 and Ezekiel 28:14.
native_notes.5:29: 'If only' renders the Hebrew optative idiom mi-yitten (literally 'Who will give'), expressing an earnest wish.
native_notes.6:4: The verbless Hebrew confession literally reads 'the LORD our God, the LORD one,' and can also be rendered 'the LORD our God, the LORD is one' or 'the LORD is our God, the LORD alone.'
native_notes.6:5: 'Might' renders Hebrew me'od, ordinarily an adverb ('very' or 'exceedingly'), here used as a noun denoting one's entire strength or capacity.
native_notes.6:7: 'Teach them repeatedly' renders the Piel of shanan (literally 'to sharpen'), denoting diligent, repeated instruction.
native_notes.6:16: Hebrew contains a wordplay between 'you tested' (nissitem, Piel of nasah) and 'Massah' (hammassah, literally 'the Testing').
native_notes.7:4: The Hiphil verb yasir, he will turn away, has a singular subject referring back to the foreign father in 7:3, and the phrase me'acharay, from following Me, shifts abruptly into first-person divine speech before returning to third-person reference to the LORD.
native_notes.7:9: The form mitsvotav, His commandments, is spelled defectively without yod in the Masoretic text here and in 8:2, a traditional ketiv/qere orthographic variant whose vocalized qere reads the plural suffix.
native_notes.7:10: The Hebrew shifts mid-clause from plural lesone'av, those who hate Him, to distributive singular el-panav leha'avido, literally to his face to destroy him, using the idiom to his face to signify direct, personal repayment.
native_notes.7:13: The rare Deuteronomic phrases shegar-alafekha, the offspring of your cattle, and ashterot tso'nekha, the young of your flock, denote livestock fertility; ashterot shares an etymology with the fertility goddess Astarte but functions here purely as a term for the young of sheep and goats.
native_notes.7:20: The singular collective noun hatsir'ah traditionally means the hornet, as in Exodus 23:28 and Joshua 24:12, though some lexicographers understand it figuratively as panic or discouragement.
native_notes.8:3: The Masoretic text reads kol-motsa pi- followed by the divine name, everything that goes forth from the mouth of the LORD, without a separate noun for word as supplied in the Septuagint and later Greek citations.
native_notes.8:7: The plural tehomot, deep waters, derives from tehom, the deep, and denotes subterranean water sources emerging as springs across the landscape.
native_notes.8:8: The construct phrase zeit shemen, literally olive of oil, refers to oil-bearing olive trees rather than wild olives.
native_notes.8:15: The collective singular phrase nachash saraf, fiery serpents, pairs nachash, serpent, with saraf from the root meaning to burn, referring to venomous snakes whose bite burns or whose appearance is fiery.
native_notes.8:20: This verse pairs the Hiphil participle ma'avid, is causing to perish, with the Qal imperfect to'vedun, you will perish, from the same root avad to underscore the parallel between the fate of the dispossessed nations and a disobedient Israel.
native_notes.9:4: In the Masoretic Hebrew, Israel's quoted inner speech ends at "this land" (1st person "my righteousness ... brought me"), after which the adversative waw introduces Moses's correction in the 2nd person ("from before you").
native_notes.9:21: "Pounded it, grinding it thoroughly" reflects the Qal wayyiqtol of katat followed by two adverbial infinitives absolute: the Qal infinitive absolute of tahan ("grinding") and the Hiphil infinitive absolute of yatav ("thoroughly").
native_notes.9:23: "Command" translates the Hebrew idiom "mouth" (pi), referring to the LORD's spoken directive.
native_notes.9:28: The singular noun "the land" (ha'arets) takes a plural verb ("will say", yo'meru) by constructio ad sensum, referring by metonymy to the inhabitants of Egypt.
native_notes.10:4: Hebrew aseret haddevarim literally means "the Ten Words" (the Decalogue), echoing "the words" (haddevarim) in 9:10 and 10:2 and distinct from "commandments" (mitswot) in 10:13.
native_notes.10:6: Verses 6-7 form a brief third-person itinerary interlude before Moses's direct address to Israel resumes in verses 9-10; "served as priest" renders the Piel denominative verb from kohen ("priest").
native_notes.10:12: The Qal participle sho'el literally means "asking," and is answered by a chain of five lamed-infinitives construct ("to fear ... to walk ... to love ... to serve ... to observe") continuing into verse 13.
native_notes.10:17: "Shows no partiality" translates the Hebrew idiom lo'-yissa' fanim, literally "does not lift up faces," meaning not favoring one party over another in judgment.
native_notes.11:2: The parenthetical Hebrew clause "for not with your children" (ki lo et-beneikhem) is elliptical, lacking an explicit verb; "I am not addressing" is supplied for clarity, while the accusative series in verses 2-6 is governed by "know" and resumed in verse 7.
native_notes.11:6: "At their feet" (be-ragleihem) is a Hebrew idiom meaning "in their train" or "following them," referring to the people and animals belonging to the company of Dathan and Abiram.
native_notes.11:13: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts into first-person divine speech in verses 13-15 ("My commandments ... I will give"), with Moses speaking directly in the voice of the LORD before returning to third-person reference to the LORD in verse 17.
native_notes.11:27: The relative particle asher here carries conditional force ("if"), standing directly parallel to im ("if") in verse 28.
native_notes.12:5: The noun rendered "His dwelling place" (shikhno, from shakhan, "to dwell") occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; the Masoretic accentuation pairs it directly with "you shall seek."
native_notes.12:12: "Within your gates" is a recurring Deuteronomic idiom (also vv. 15, 17, 18, 21) denoting "in your towns" or "within your local settlements."
native_notes.12:22: The Niphal passive verb ye'akhel ("is eaten") governs direct-object markers before its logical subjects ("the gazelle and the deer"), a classic impersonal passive construction in Biblical Hebrew (literally "as one eats the gazelle and the deer").
native_notes.12:30: "Ensnared into following them" renders a pregnant Hebrew construction (tinnaqesh achareihem, Niphal of naqash, literally "be ensnared after them").
native_notes.13:1: The Masoretic Text begins chapter 13 with this verse; in the verse division of the Latin Vulgate tradition it is 12:32, and the remaining verses of chapter 13 are numbered one lower there.
native_notes.13:6: The Hiphil of nadach (literally "thrust/drive away") is used consistently in vv. 6, 11, and 14 for driving or leading someone astray from faithfulness to the LORD. Here sarah ("rebellion") literally denotes turning aside or defection.
native_notes.13:14: Hebrew anashim bene-beliyya'al is literally "men, sons of worthlessness" (or "wickedness"). The same noun beliyya'al recurs in 15:9 for a "worthless" thought.
native_notes.13:16: The Hiphil infinitive absolute hacharem ("devoting to destruction," from charam) denotes placing persons or property under the irreversible ban (cherem, v. 18) dedicated to the LORD. In v. 17, kalil ("whole offering") is a sacrificial term for an offering consumed entirely by fire.
native_notes.14:5: The exact zoological identifications of several wild ruminants in this list—especially yachmur ("fallow deer"), aqqo ("wild goat"), dishon ("addax"), teo ("oryx"), and zamer ("mountain sheep")—remain uncertain.
native_notes.14:8: Hebrew velo gerah is elliptical (literally "and not cud"), omitting the participle for chewing/bringing up the cud from v. 7.
native_notes.14:13: The Masoretic Text lists three birds here (ra'ah, ayyah, and dayyah), whereas the parallel list in Leviticus 11:14 has two (da'ah and ayyah); exact species identifications for many of the unclean birds in vv. 12-18 are uncertain.
native_notes.14:21: Hebrew nevelah refers specifically to the carcass of an animal that died naturally rather than by slaughter (compare "their carcasses" in v. 8). The Qal infinitive absolute makhor ("sell") functions permissively alongside the finite verb tittenennah ("you may give it").
native_notes.15:2: The Qal infinitive absolute shamot ("release") functions jussively, followed by kol-ba'al mashsheh yado, literally "every holder of a loan of his hand" (that is, every creditor). In the final clause, the indefinite third-person verb qara ("one has proclaimed") is rendered passively ("has been proclaimed").
native_notes.15:6: Hebrew contrasts two stems of the same verb avat ("give or take a pledge"): the Hiphil veha'avatta ("you will lend") and the Qal lo ta'avot ("you will not borrow"), with the Hiphil recurring in v. 8.
native_notes.15:9: Hebrew vera'ah enekha (literally "and your eye is evil") is an idiom for stinginess or hostility; the same Qal verb ra'a ("be evil/begrudging") recurs in v. 10 with the heart (lo-yera levavekha).
native_notes.15:14: The Hiphil infinitive absolute and imperfect ha'aneq ta'aniq ("supply generously") derive from anaq ("necklace"), occurring in the Hiphil only here in the Hebrew Bible with the sense of adorning or loading someone generously with provisions.
native_notes.15:18: Hebrew mishneh sekhar sakhir literally means "double the wages of a hired worker," indicating that six years of continuous bondservice yielded twice the value of hiring a laborer (some interpret mishneh here as "equivalent to").
native_notes.16:5: Hebrew she'arekha ("your gates") is used metonymically throughout Deuteronomy for Israel's walled towns and settlements (compare 16:11, 14, 18; 17:2, 8; 18:6).
native_notes.16:7: The Piel verb bishalta (from bashal) commonly denotes boiling or cooking more broadly, rendered here generally as "cook."
native_notes.16:10: Hebrew missat ("the measure of") is a hapax legomenon occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible, denoting sufficiency, measure, or proportion (cognate with Aramaic missat, "enough").
native_notes.16:16: The Masoretic text vocalizes yera'eh as a Niphal ("be seen / appear") followed by the direct-object marker et-pene ("the face of"), a recurring festival idiom that some grammarians view as a reverential vocalization of an original Qal ("see the face of").
native_notes.16:20: Hebrew repeats the noun (tsedeq tsedeq, "justice, justice") for emphatic intensity and exclusivity, conveying "justice and nothing but justice."
native_notes.17:3: The text shifts abruptly to first-person divine speech (lo-tsivviti, Piel perfect of tsavah, "which I have not commanded") without a quotation formula.
native_notes.17:8: The three paired expressions cover difficult judicial distinctions involving homicide ("blood and blood," dam), civil or legal claims ("lawsuit and lawsuit," din), and physical assault or skin affliction ("blow and blow," nega').
native_notes.17:9: "The Levitical priests" translates the characteristic Deuteronomic appositional phrase ha-kohanim ha-leviyyim, literally "the priests, the Levites" (compare 17:18; 18:1).
native_notes.17:18: Hebrew mishneh ha-torah ha-zot means "a copy/duplicate of this law" (rendered in the Septuagint as to deuteronomion touto, "this second law," whence the English name Deuteronomy). The compound preposition millifne ("from before") indicates copying from the authoritative scroll kept by the Levitical priests.
native_notes.18:1: "His inheritance" (ve-nachalato) refers to the sacred dues, offerings, and portions belonging to the LORD that are allotted to the tribe of Levi for sustenance.
native_notes.18:8: Hebrew levad mimkarav al-ha'avot literally reads "apart from his sales upon/concerning the fathers," a compressed legal phrase referring to personal proceeds from the sale of patrimonial holdings.
native_notes.18:10: Verses 10-11 use technical participial forms for forbidden occult practices, including me'onen (Polel participle, "soothsayer/augur"), menachesh (Piel participle, "omen reader"), chover chaver ("binder/caster of spells"), and sho'el ov ve-yid'oni ("inquirer of a ghost/medium or familiar spirit").
native_notes.18:22: "You shall not dread him" translates the Qal imperfect lo tagur mimmennu (from gur II, "stand in dread/awe of"), a stronger term for fearful deference than the more general yare' ("fear").
native_notes.19:4: Literally "without knowledge" and "from yesterday and the third day," standard Hebrew idioms for acting accidentally and having no prior hostility.
native_notes.19:10: Hebrew damim (plural of dam, "blood") denotes culpability for shed blood, appearing here with a singular verb.
native_notes.19:16: "Malicious witness" is literally "a witness of violence," referring to one who gives false testimony to inflict unjust harm.
native_notes.20:6: The Piel verb hillel (literally "make common") refers to releasing the produce of a new vineyard for ordinary consumption after its initial consecrated period (cf. Lev 19:23-25).
native_notes.20:8: The Masoretic verb yimmas is Niphal ("melt") followed by the direct object marker et before "the heart of his brothers," an unusual construction where et introduces the subject of a passive/intransitive verb (or else the verb is read causatively, "he will not make the heart of his brothers melt").
native_notes.20:19: Although ha-adam is pointed with the definite article rather than an interrogative prefix, the clause is widely understood as an unmarked rhetorical question (literally "For is the human being a tree of the field, to come from before you into the siege?").
native_notes.21:7: Translating the Masoretic qere shafekhu (3rd-person common plural, matching dual "our hands"); the ketiv shafekhah has a feminine singular or archaic feminine plural ending.
native_notes.21:8: "Shall be atoned for" renders a rare Nithpael (hybrid Niphal-Hithpael passive-reflexive) form of kafar ("atone").
native_notes.21:12: "Trim her nails" is literally "do" or "tend her nails"; the idiom usually means paring the nails (cf. 2 Sam 19:24), though some ancient interpreters understood it as letting them grow as a sign of mourning.
native_notes.21:14: The rare Hithpael verb hit-ammer (occurring only here and Deut 24:7) denotes treating someone harshly, exploiting them, or dealing with them as a slave.
native_notes.21:23: The Hebrew construct "a curse of God" (qillelat elohim) may be understood either as a subjective genitive ("cursed by God") or as an objective genitive ("an affront to God").
native_notes.22:5: Hebrew keli-gever ('an article/equipment of a man') is broader than simlah ('garment') in the second clause and can encompass male attire, accessories, or gear.
native_notes.22:9: Hebrew tiqdash (Qal imperfect of qadash) literally means 'will become holy/consecrated,' referring to produce forfeited to the sanctuary and thus forbidden for ordinary use.
native_notes.22:11: Hebrew shaatnez is a technical term for mixed-fiber fabric, immediately defined here as wool and linen combined together.
native_notes.22:14: Hebrew alilot devarim (lit. 'pretexts/deeds of words,' recurring in v. 17) denotes trumped-up or baseless accusations.
native_notes.22:15: Here and in vv. 16, 20-21, and 23-29 (unlike v. 19), the consonantal text writes the archaic Pentateuchal form naar without final he, vocalized as a qere perpetuum for feminine naarah ('young woman').
native_notes.23:1: Hebrew kenaph aviv literally means 'the wing/corner of his father,' referring to the corner of a garment or covering as an idiom for marital rights and intimacy (cf. Ruth 3:9).
native_notes.23:3: Hebrew mamzer (occurring only here and in Zech 9:6) denotes someone born of an illicit or forbidden union; its exact legal scope is debated.
native_notes.23:5: Hebrew sakhar ('he hired') is singular, referring specifically to Moab, though rendered 'they hired' to agree with the plural verb earlier in the verse. Aram-naharaim literally means 'Aram of the Two Rivers,' i.e., Upper Mesopotamia.
native_notes.23:14: Hebrew azenekha ('your equipment/gear') is a hapax legomenon whose exact sense is uncertain, commonly understood as personal tools, weapons, or field gear.
native_notes.23:18: Hebrew qedeshah (fem.) and qadesh (masc.) literally mean 'consecrated woman' and 'consecrated man,' referring to cultic personnel associated with illicit sexual rites, paired with 'prostitute' and 'dog' (likely a contemptuous metaphor for a male prostitute) in v. 19.
native_notes.23:25: Native Masoretic order places the vineyard law at 23:25 and the standing-grain law at 23:26 (corresponding to 23:24–25 in alternative versifications); in the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 23:25 maps to slot 23:26 and MT 23:26 maps to slot 23:25.
native_notes.24:1: Hebrew erwat dabar literally means "nakedness of a matter," an idiom denoting something indecent or improper. Verses 1-3 form a single extended conditional protasis whose legal prohibition appears in verse 4.
native_notes.24:4: The verb rendered "has been defiled" is the rare Hothpaal passive-reflexive perfect of the root meaning to be unclean, emphasizing that the woman is regarded as defiled with respect to her first husband.
native_notes.24:7: The Hithpael verb hit'ammer, occurring only here and in Deuteronomy 21:14, denotes treating a captive brutally, tyrannically, or as a slave.
native_notes.24:20: The Piel verb tefa'er is a denominative from po'rah, meaning "bough" or "branch," and denotes going back through the olive branches a second time.
native_notes.25:2: Hebrew bin hakkot literally means "a son of striking," using the Hiphil infinitive construct of the verb to strike as an idiom for deserving a beating.
native_notes.25:5: The Piel verb yibbem, appearing here and in verse 7, is a denominative from yabam, "husband's brother," denoting the levirate duty of marrying a deceased brother's childless widow to preserve his line.
native_notes.25:13: Hebrew eben wa'aben, literally "a stone and a stone," and efah we'efah in verse 14, literally "an ephah and an ephah," use repetition to denote dishonest dual standards for scale weights and dry grain measures.
native_notes.25:18: The Piel verb wayzanneb is a denominative from zanab, "tail," meaning to cut off the rear of a marching column; hanneheshalim is a Niphal participle occurring only here in Biblical Hebrew, denoting those who are feeble or lagging behind.
native_notes.26:5: Hebrew arammi obed uses the Qal active participle of the verb meaning to perish or be lost, literally "a perishing Aramean," also widely understood as "a wandering Aramean" referring to Jacob's vulnerable nomadic state or famine-driven descent into Egypt.
native_notes.26:12: The form la'ser is a syncopated Hiphil infinitive construct of the verb meaning to tithe, denoting the formal setting aside or delivery of the third-year tithe.
native_notes.26:14: Hebrew be'oni, "during my mourning," derives from a noun meaning sorrow or mourning as in Hosea 9:4, a state that rendered consecrated food ritually unfit to eat.
native_notes.26:17: The Hiphil of the verb meaning "to say," he'emarta here and he'emireka in verse 18, occurs only in these two verses in the Hebrew Bible, expressing a solemn mutual covenantal affirmation or eliciting of a pledge between Israel and the LORD.
native_notes.27:4: The Masoretic Text reads "on Mount Ebal," whereas the Samaritan Pentateuch reads "on Mount Gerizim."
native_notes.27:8: "clearly and thoroughly" renders two adverbial infinitives absolute: the Piel infinitive absolute of ba'ar ("make plain/clear") and the Hiphil infinitive absolute of yatav ("do well/thoroughly").
native_notes.27:9: "Keep silent" renders the Hiphil imperative of sakat, a word occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible, calling for hushed attention.
native_notes.27:20: "uncovered the edge of his father's garment" renders a Hebrew idiom (literally "uncovered his father's wing/hem," cf. Deut 23:1) denoting the violation of his father's marital bed.
native_notes.27:26: The Masoretic Text reads "the words of this law" without "all" (contrast vv. 3 and 8), whereas the Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint include "all."
native_notes.28:22: The Masoretic vocalization reads cherev ('sword'); an alternate vocalization of the same consonants, chorev, means 'drought,' which aligns with the surrounding climatic and crop afflictions.
native_notes.28:25: After plural 'your enemies,' the Hebrew shifts to collective masculine singular suffixes (literally 'against him ... before him'), rendered 'them' for English agreement.
native_notes.28:27: The ketiv reads ba'ophalim ('with swellings' or 'with tumors'); the Masoretic qere substitutes the euphemistic battechorim ('with hemorrhoids'), followed in the translation.
native_notes.28:30: The ketiv reads yishgalennah ('will violate/ravish her'); the Masoretic qere substitutes the euphemistic yishkavennah ('will lie with her'), followed here. In the final clause, the Piel verb chalal literally means 'make common' or 'deconsecrate,' referring to harvesting a new vineyard's fruit for ordinary use (cf. Lev 19:23-25; Deut 20:6).
native_notes.28:32: The clause 'there will be no power in your hand' renders the Hebrew idiom 'ein le'el yadekha (literally 'there is not in the strength of your hand'), expressing complete helplessness.
native_notes.28:42: 'The cricket' translates the rare noun tselatsal, derived from a root meaning 'to buzz' or 'whirr,' referring to a buzzing locust or cricket; yeyaresh is the sole Piel occurrence of yarash ('possess, take over') in the Hebrew Bible.
native_notes.28:48: After plural 'your enemies,' Hebrew uses a collective masculine singular suffix on yeshallechennu (literally 'whom the LORD will send him'). The subject of 'He will place ... until He destroys' is the LORD.
native_notes.28:54: 'His eye will turn begrudging' renders the Hebrew idiom tera' 'eino (literally 'his eye will be evil toward,' repeated in v. 56), denoting extreme stinginess and hostility.
native_notes.28:66: 'Will hang in suspense' translates telu'im (Qal passive participle of tala', a by-form of talah, 'hang'), portraying life as hanging precariously in constant uncertainty.
native_notes.28:68: 'You will put yourselves up for sale' translates the Hithpael hitmakkartem (conative reflexive of makar, 'sell'), vividly depicting desperate self-enslavement that fails because no one will buy.
native_notes.29:4: Here and in v. 5 ("I led you... I am the LORD your God"), Moses shifts abruptly from third-person reference to the LORD (vv. 1-3) into first-person divine speech before returning to first-person plural with Israel ("us... we") in v. 6.
native_notes.29:8: "succeed" translates the Hiphil of sakal, which encompasses both acting wisely and achieving success as the fruit of wisdom.
native_notes.29:9: The Masoretic text attaches the second-person plural suffix to both nouns (rashekem shivtekem, "your heads, your tribes"), either listing them in series or placing "your tribes" in apposition to "your heads" (unlike the construct reading "heads of your tribes" in the Septuagint and Samaritan Pentateuch).
native_notes.29:18: "so as to sweep away the watered with the dry" renders the Qal infinitive construct of saphah with two feminine adjectives (haravah and hatsemeah), probably a merism for total devastation; Hebrew alah ("sworn curse" here and in vv. 19-20, 30:7) denotes a covenant oath backed by imprecations (rendered "oath" in vv. 11, 13).
native_notes.29:28: In the Masoretic text, extraordinary dots (puncta extraordinaria) mark the ten letters of lanu ulevanenu ("to us and to our children") and the first letter (ayin) of ad ("forever"), an ancient scribal marking whose original significance is debated.
native_notes.30:3: "restore your fortunes" renders the Hebrew idiom shuv shevut (Qal of shuv with the cognate noun shevut), meaning to reverse a condition and restore former well-being, while playing acoustically on captivity (root shavah) in exilic contexts.
native_notes.30:11: "not beyond you" translates the Niphal participle of pala with the preposition min ("too extraordinary/difficult for you"), denoting what exceeds human grasp or capability.
native_notes.30:16: The Masoretic text begins directly with the conjunction asher ("in that") linking to v. 15, without the longer conditional clause ("If you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God") found in the Septuagint.
native_notes.30:18: "certainly perish" renders the emphatic Qal infinitive absolute paired with the Qal imperfect of avad (avod tovedun), underscoring the certainty of destruction.
native_notes.31:6: The Hiphil verb from rph literally means 'let go of' or 'drop', paired with Qal azav ('abandon'), the same verb that recurs in verses 8, 16, and 17.
native_notes.31:7: MT reads Qal imperfect tavo ('you will go') with the preposition et ('with'), contrasting with verse 23, which uses Hiphil tavi ('you will bring') with the direct object marker et.
native_notes.31:11: MT points the infinitive construct as Niphal leraot ('to appear'), with et-pene functioning adverbially as 'in the presence of' or 'before'.
native_notes.31:19: The Hebrew imperatives shift from second-person masculine plural ('write ... for yourselves', addressing both Moses and Joshua) to second-person masculine singular (Piel 'teach it' and Qal 'place it', addressing Moses).
native_notes.31:23: MT supplies no explicit subject noun for the verb 'commissioned'; the first-person divine promises ('I swore ... I Myself will be with you') and the fulfillment of verse 14 identify the speaker as the LORD.
native_notes.32:5: The Masoretic syntax is condensed and difficult, literally reading "acted corruptly toward Him, not His children, their blemish," with the singular Piel verb שִׁחֵת referring to Israel collectively.
native_notes.32:8: The Masoretic Text reads "the sons of Israel" (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), whereas a Dead Sea Scroll manuscript (4QDeutj) reads "sons of God" and the Septuagint reads "angels of God."
native_notes.32:13: Ketiv במותי and qere בָּמֳתֵי represent an orthographic variant in the construct plural of בָּמָה ("heights" or "high places"), with the qere omitting the vav; both carry the same meaning.
native_notes.32:26: The hapax verb אַפְאֵיהֶם (Hiphil imperfect 1cs of פאה with 3mp suffix) is understood either as "cleave them in pieces" or, denominatively from פֵּאָה ("corner, edge"), as "scatter them to the corners."
native_notes.32:28: Hebrew has no quotation marks; closing the quotation at v. 27 reflects the shift from first-person divine speech (vv. 20–27) to third-person reflection and first-person plural ("our Rock," v. 31), though some interpreters extend the LORD's speech through v. 29 or v. 33. The referent of "they" across vv. 28–33 (Israel vs. Israel's enemies) is likewise debated.
native_notes.32:34: Hebrew introduces no new speech formula here, though the abrupt return to first-person singular pronouns ("with Me," "My storehouses," "Mine" in vv. 34–35) marks a resumption of divine speech before third-person narration returns in v. 36.
native_notes.32:43: In the Masoretic Text, the Hiphil imperative הַרְנִינוּ takes עַמּוֹ ("His people") directly without a preposition ("Acclaim His people, nations"), and אַדְמָתוֹ עַמּוֹ ("His land, His people") is asyndetic; 4QDeutq and the Septuagint preserve longer texts with additional lines.
native_notes.33:2: Ketiv/Qere: the ketiv is written as one word (אשדת, often taken as "fiery slopes" or "flashing fire"), while the qere divides it into two words (אֵשׁ דָּת, "fire of law," i.e., "a fiery law"), which is translated here. Also, "myriads of holy ones" renders מֵרִבְבֹת קֹדֶשׁ (literally "from myriads of holiness").
native_notes.33:3: The verb תֻּכּוּ is a hapax legomenon (usually parsed as a Pual perfect of an uncertain root תכה), understood as "settled down" or "followed closely" at Your feet. The following verb יִשָּׂא is third-person masculine singular, used distributively ("each one receives").
native_notes.33:6: Literally the second clause reads "and let his men be a number" (מִסְפָּר, idiomatically "few in number"); the negative particle אַל ("not") from the preceding jussive is understood to carry over by poetic ellipsis, though some read it concessively ("though his men be few").
native_notes.33:12: The antecedents of the third-person masculine singular pronouns in the final clause (וּבֵין כְּתֵפָיו שָׁכֵן) are ambiguous: either the LORD dwells between Benjamin's shoulders (evoking the slopes/ridges of Benjamin's territory), as rendered here, or Benjamin dwells securely between the LORD's shoulders.
native_notes.33:25: Both מִנְעָלֶךָ ("your bolts," from נעל "to lock/bolt," though anciently also understood as "your sandals") and דׇּבְאֶךָ (understood as "your strength," or by some comparative Semitic scholars "your security/rest") are hapax legomena in Biblical Hebrew.
native_notes.34:5: "At the LORD's command" translates the Hebrew idiom עַל־פִּי יְהֹוָה, literally "by the mouth of the LORD."
native_notes.34:6: The verb וַיִּקְבֹּר is a third-person masculine singular active Qal wayyiqtol ("and He buried him"), with the LORD as the understood subject, though it is sometimes interpreted impersonally ("he was buried").
native_notes.34:7: The noun לֵחֹה ("his vitality," from לֵחַ, literally "moisture" or "freshness") is a hapax legomenon with the archaic third-person masculine singular suffix -ֹה, and the verb נָס literally means "fled."
